content: 配套部署脚本已开源至 windcicada/OrangePi_Kunpeng_Router。 仓库只保存可公开的脚本和简要说明；这篇文章是完整部署教程，包含硬件约定、执行顺序、 验收方法和失联恢复步骤。 本文记录一套已经在 Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 上完成家庭 PPPoE、NAT、DHCP、DNS 和重启恢复验收的软路由配置。文中的账号、密码、物理 MAC 和公网地址均使用 占位符；请勿把设备上的真实配置直接提交到 Git。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 1. 最终效果 这套方案不把 OpenWrt 直接刷进 Kunpeng Pro，而是保留厂商 openEuler 作为宿主， 再用 ARM64 KVM 虚拟机运行 OpenWrt。这样可以同时保留板级驱动，以及 OpenWrt 的 LuCI、UCI 和 firewall4 配置能力。 完成后： 光猫桥接，OpenWrt VM 负责 PPPoE、NAT、DHCP 和 DNS。 Intel I226-V 网卡作为 WAN；Kunpeng Pro 板载 HNS3 网口作为 LAN。 小米路由器改为有线中继/AP，只负责 Wi-Fi 和交换，不再拨号、NAT 或发 DHCP。 openEuler 宿主保留 192.168.50.2 救援地址；OpenWrt LuCI 为 http://192.168.50.1/。 宿主断电重启后，双桥、libvirt 网络、OpenWrt VM 和 WAN 选择器自动恢复。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content:

title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 3. 已验证环境 组件 已验证版本/状态 Kunpeng Pro 宿主 openEuler 22.03 LTS-SP4，内核 5.10.0+ OpenWrt 25.12.1，armsr/armv8，ext4 combined EFI 虚拟化 KVM/QEMU/libvirt，VM 2 vCPU、1 GiB RAM、4 GiB raw 磁盘 Intel 网卡 I226-V，PCI ID 8086:125c，自建 igc.ko LAN 192.168.50.0/24，DHCP 192.168.50.100-249 PPPoE MTU 1480、IPv4、默认路由和对端 DNS启用 OpenWrt 25.12 及更新版本使用 apk 包管理器，不再使用 opkg。OpenWrt 官方也明确 警告不要用 apk upgrade 对系统做盲目全量升级；系统升级应使用匹配版本的固件。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 4. 硬件和救援条件 准备： Kunpeng Pro、电源、散热、可启动的 TF 卡和 eMMC。 M.2 M Key/B+M Key、PCIe x1 的 Intel I226-V 网卡。 Micro USB 调试线，串口参数 115200 8N1。 一台有有线网口的电脑。 处于桥接模式的光猫、运营商 PPPoE 凭据。 作为下游 AP 的路由器或交换机。 所有桥接切换、写盘和首次 VM 网络配置都应在 HDMI/键盘或串口可用时执行。SSH 断开不等于系统死机；网络切换过程中失去远程入口是正常风险。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 5. 获取镜像并写入 eMMC 从 Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 官方资料页 获取 Kunpeng Pro 对应的 openEuler 镜像、手册和源码。 用 TF 卡启动，确认根分区确实是 /dev/mmcblk1p1，eMMC 是 /dev/mmcblk0 且未挂载。 对下载文件执行 sha256sum 和 xz -t，并记录哈希。 使用 05-flash-emmc.sh： IMAGE=/root/Kunpeng-openEuler.img.xz \ I_UNDERSTAND=YES \ bash ./05-flash-emmc.sh 该脚本会拒绝从非 TF 根系统写 eMMC，也会拒绝覆盖已挂载的目标。写入期间不得 断电、重启或拔卡。完成后正常关机，移除 TF 卡，切换为 eMMC 启动，再验收： findmnt -no SOURCE / lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS,UUID systemctl is-active sshd NetworkManager 预期根分区是 /dev/mmcblk0p1。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 6. 恢复 Intel I226-V 驱动 原厂内核可枚举 8086:125c，但当前内核配置没有提供可加载的 IGC 模块。已验证的 做法是使用与运行内核严格匹配的完整开发树和 Module.symvers，只编译 IGC： uname -r lspci -nnk -s 01:00.0 test -f /usr/src/kernels/"$(uname -r)"/Module.symvers bash ./00-build-igc.sh 脚本的核心命令是： make -C /usr/src/kernels/"$(uname -r)" \ M=drivers/net/ethernet/intel/igc CONFIG_IGC=m modules 成功后模块位于 /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/extra/igc.ko，并由 /etc/modules-load.d/igc.conf 开机加载。验收： modinfo igc | grep -E 'filename|vermagic' lspci -nnk -s 01:00.0 ip -br link ethtool -i eth0 vermagic 必须与 uname -r 一致。出现 Key was rejected、未知符号或版本不匹配时 立即停止；不要使用 --force 强行加载。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 板载 HNS3 的特殊依赖 Kunpeng Pro 板载口使用厂商 hclgeplf.ko，它依赖 Ascend 的 DFM、blackbox、QoS、 DMS 等符号，不能只靠标准内核的 hns3.ko 独立恢复。因此： 使用板载口时不要删除 /var/davinci，也不要屏蔽 start-davinci.service。 不要在远程会话里试卸载整套 Ascend 内核模块；这台板曾因此卡住重启。 某些厂商线程会使 Linux load average 很高，但 CPU 仍有 95% 以上空闲。判断性能 要看 top 的 CPU idle、软中断、延迟和丢包，不能只看 load average。 如果必须彻底移除厂商栈，应放弃板载 HNS3，改用受主线内核支持的 USB 3.0 RTL8153/AX88179 网卡作为 LAN。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 7. 创建宿主双桥 先确认物理角色： for i in eth0 eth1; do printf '%s mac=%s driver=' "$i" "$(cat /sys/class/net/$i/address)" basename "$(readlink -f /sys/class/net/$i/device/driver)" ethtool "$i" | grep -E 'Speed|Link detected' done 在已验证硬件映射后运行： WAN_IF=eth0 LAN_IF=eth1 LAN_HOST_CIDR=192.168.50.2/24 \ bash ./10-configure-host-bridges.sh 脚本只创建/修改配置，不会自动切断现有连接。它会输出需要从串口执行的激活命令。 激活前，应把占用 eth0/eth1 的旧 NetworkManager 配置设为不自动连接： nmcli connection show nmcli connection modify '<旧连接名>' connection.autoconnect no 然后从串口依次启用 LAN、WAN： nmcli connection up br-lan nmcli connection up br-lan-port ifname eth1 nmcli connection up br-wan nmcli connection up br-wan-port ifname eth0 验收： ip -br addr show br-wan ip -br addr show br-lan bridge link nmcli -f NAME,TYPE,DEVICE,AUTOCONNECT connection show 正确状态是 br-wan 没有宿主 IPv4，br-lan 为 192.168.50.2/24，四个 bridge 和 port 配置均自动连接。宿主默认路由不应出现在 br-wan。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 8. 创建 OpenWrt KVM 虚拟机 从 OpenWrt 25.12.1 armsr/armv8 官方目录 下载 generic-ext4-combined-efi.img.gz 并核对官方 SHA-256。本文验收版本的哈希是： 43e04e13c03b191f666a64bf4a601fa7645bc7aacaca3a580b1b6f5394c74de3 未来发布新版本时应改用对应目录中当时的哈希，不要继续照抄旧值。 确认 KVM 和固件： test -c /dev/kvm ls -l /usr/share/edk2/aarch64/QEMU_EFI-pflash.raw systemctl enable --now libvirtd 创建 VM： IMAGE_GZ=/root/openwrt-25.12.1-armsr-armv8-generic-ext4-combined-efi.img.gz \ IMAGE_SHA256=43e04e13c03b191f666a64bf4a601fa7645bc7aacaca3a580b1b6f5394c74de3 \ bash ./20-create-openwrt-vm.sh 脚本会： 将 ext4 EFI 镜像解压为 raw 磁盘并扩到 4 GiB。 创建 openwrt-lan -> br-lan 和 openwrt-wan -> br-wan 两个纯桥接 libvirt 网络。 创建 2 vCPU、1 GiB RAM、virtio 磁盘/网卡、AArch64 UEFI 的 VM。 为 LAN/WAN 固定虚拟 MAC，设置 VM 和两个虚拟网络自动启动。 打开串口控制台；退出控制台按 Ctrl+]。 libvirt 使用现有 Linux bridge 的方式可参阅其 Network XML 官方文档。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 9. 配置 OpenWrt LAN、DHCP、PPPoE 和自动上游切换 把这些文件复制到 OpenWrt 的同一目录： 30-configure-openwrt.sh wan-mode wan-mode.init wanmode.uci 从 OpenWrt 串口执行： sh ./30-configure-openwrt.sh 脚本会在终端中静默读取 PPPoE 密码，不把凭据写入脚本或命令行历史；如果已有值， 直接回车即可保留。首次网络 reload 后，管理地址会从 OpenWrt 默认地址变成 192.168.50.1。 wan-mode 的逻辑是： auto 模式先启动 DHCP WAN。 DHCP 获得地址、默认路由且直连健康检查通过时，保持 DHCP。 DHCP 不健康时停止 DHCP，启动 PPPoE。 PPPoE 健康后保持连接；链路失效时重新选择。 失败重试使用 30、60、120、300 秒退避，避免高频拨号。 命令： wan-mode status wan-mode dhcp wan-mode pppoe wan-mode auto 家庭长期使用保持 auto 即可。若不需要办公室/校园 DHCP 兼容，也可以固定执行 wan-mode pppoe。示例配置默认关闭校园认证；只有部署者另行提供 /usr/sbin/wan-campus-auth 并明确开启后才会调用。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 关键防火墙修复：必须把 PPPoE 放进 WAN zone 这是整个部署中最容易遗漏、影响又最大的配置。OpenWrt 的防火墙 zone 按“逻辑 network 接口”分组，不是只按物理 eth1 分组。实际三层出口是 pppoe-wanpppoe，所以 WAN zone 必须包含 wanpppoe： uci show firewall | grep -E "name='wan'|network=.*wanpppoe" 期望的配置语义： WAN zone networks: wan wan6 wanpppoe WAN input: REJECT WAN output: ACCEPT WAN forward: DROP WAN masquerading: enabled WAN MTU fix: enabled LAN -> WAN forwarding: enabled 遗漏 wanpppoe 时，普通 UDP 转发可能被 firewall4 丢弃，部分依赖 UDP 的应用会出现 高延迟或连接不稳定。修复后应重新检查 WAN zone、NAT、MSS 修正和 UDP 连通性。 OpenWrt 官方说明 zone 的 network 字段就是该 zone 包含的接口列表，WAN masquerade 和 MSS clamping 也在 zone 级别生效。参阅 OpenWrt firewall 配置文档。 不要执行 uci show network.wanpppoe，它会把账号和密码打印出来。只检查字段是否 存在： test -n "$(uci -q get network.wanpppoe.username)" && echo username_present=yes test -n "$(uci -q get network.wanpppoe.password)" && echo password_present=yes
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 10. 小米路由器切换为有线中继/AP 必须先让电脑直连 Kunpeng LAN，并确认 PPPoE、DHCP 和 DNS 全部正常，再调整小米： Kunpeng 板载 LAN 接小米任一自动 WAN/LAN 口。 先让小米使用 DHCP，确认它从 OpenWrt 获得 192.168.50.x 并能联网。 再切换为“有线中继/AP”。 终端应直接从 OpenWrt 获得地址，默认网关和 DNS 都是 192.168.50.1。 在 OpenWrt 的 DHCP 租约中找到小米，必要时固定为 192.168.50.3。 小米不再 PPPoE、不再 NAT、不再发 DHCP。不要同时让 OpenWrt 和小米在同一 LAN 上 发 DHCP。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 11. 自启和稳定性验收 宿主机： bash ./90-verify-host.sh systemctl is-enabled NetworkManager libvirtd virsh net-list --all virsh dominfo openwrt-router | grep -E 'State|Autostart' OpenWrt： sh ./91-verify-openwrt.sh /etc/init.d/wan-mode enabled 做一次受控重启，重启后等待 1–2 分钟，再确认： br-lan、br-wan 和两个物理 port 都自动连接。 openwrt-lan、openwrt-wan 和 openwrt-router 自动启动。 wan-mode status 最终为 active_mode=pppoe、last_result=ok。 LAN 终端能获取地址，DHCP、DNS 和普通 UDP 转发均正常。 这台板上 vendor D-state 线程可能抬高 load average。只要 CPU 大部分时间空闲、没有 持续 softirq 满核、丢包或明显延迟，2 vCPU/1 GiB 的 OpenWrt VM 对当前用途有足够 余量。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 12. 备份、升级和回滚
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 备份 OpenWrt： sysupgrade -b /tmp/openwrt-config-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz 宿主： virsh dumpxml openwrt-router > /root/openwrt-router.xml virsh net-dumpxml openwrt-lan > /root/openwrt-lan.xml virsh net-dumpxml openwrt-wan > /root/openwrt-wan.xml nmcli connection show > /root/network-connections.txt OpenWrt 备份可能含 PPPoE 密码和本机网络配置，只能加密离线保存，不能公开。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 升级 不执行 apk upgrade 全量升级 OpenWrt。 升级前备份，使用同 target 的新固件，并确认自定义软件包与新版本兼容。 宿主内核变更后，旧 igc.ko 可能失配，必须用新内核的源码树和 Module.symvers 重建。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 网络失联恢复 接入串口 115200 8N1，登录 openEuler。 检查 ip -br addr、nmcli device status、bridge link。 检查 virsh domstate openwrt-router；必要时 virsh start openwrt-router。 用 virsh console openwrt-router 进入 OpenWrt；退出按 Ctrl+]。 先恢复 br-lan=192.168.50.2/24 和 OpenWrt 192.168.50.1，再处理 WAN。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: IGC 回滚 rm -f /etc/modules-load.d/igc.conf rm -f /lib/modules/"$(uname -r)"/extra/igc.ko depmod -a reboot 如果 I226-V 无法稳定工作，使用受 Linux ARM64 支持的 USB 3.0 网卡替代，不要强制 加载失配模块。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 13. 禁止事项 不把 PPPoE 账号、密码或设备导出的真实网络配置写进 Git。 不公开 /etc/config/network、/etc/config/firewall 或完整 OpenWrt sysupgrade 备份。 不把 br-wan 配成宿主管理口，不从 WAN 开放 LuCI/SSH。 不交换已确认的物理 WAN/LAN 角色，不把两个物理口加入同一个 bridge。 不强制加载 vermagic 不匹配或签名失败的内核模块。 不在使用板载 HNS3 时移除厂商 Ascend 驱动依赖。 不在缺少串口救援时执行桥接切换、驱动卸载或远程重启测试。 不用 load average 单一指标判断板子是否过载。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: 14. 发布前脱敏 只发布本目录和 scripts/kunpeng-router/ 中列出的文件。不要把本机工作目录整体推送。 发布前执行： rg -n -i \ 'password|passwd|username|authorized_keys|100\\.[0-9]+\\.|ENC:' \ docs/kunpeng-router scripts/kunpeng-router 逐项确认命中只来自说明文字、变量名或占位符，没有真实值。还应人工检查公网 IP、 手机号、邮箱、物理 MAC、SSH 指纹和家庭 DDNS。 相关脚本采用 MIT License；教程正文可由发布网站按其内容许可处理。官方参考： Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 官方资料 OpenWrt 25.12.1 armsr/armv8 下载目录 OpenWrt apk 包管理器 OpenWrt firewall 配置 libvirt Network XML 本文配套脚本和精简项目说明见 OrangePi_Kunpeng_Router GitHub 仓库。
title: Orange Pi Kunpeng Pro 双网口 OpenWrt 软路由配置实录

content: Overview This article presents an open-source 2-D compressible shear-layer DNS solver designed for studying turbulence-chemistry interactions and validating the Turbulence-Chemistry Recursive (TCR) micro-mixing model. The code is available on GitHub: github.com/windcicada/shearlayer-combustion-DNS
title: ShearLayer-Combustion DNS: A Compressible 2-D Shear Layer DNS Solver for TCR Model Validation

content: 1. Physical Background
title: ShearLayer-Combustion DNS: A Compressible 2-D Shear Layer DNS Solver for TCR Model Validation

content: The Temporal Shear Layer The temporally-developing shear layer is a canonical configuration for turbulence-chemistry interaction studies. Two streams with different velocities mix through Kelvin–Helmholtz instability, generating a turbulent mixing layer that grows in time. DNS velocity field with vorticity overlay at t = 100, showing shear-layer roll-up and vortex pairing.The key advantage of this configuration for TCR validation: Well-defined inlet conditions — no inflow turbulence generation Self-similar growth — the mixing layer width grows as $\delta(t) \propto t$ Strong scalar mixing — passive and reactive scalars mix through the evolving turbulence field Controllable chemistry — simple Arrhenius-type reaction models link directly to DNS resolution
title: ShearLayer-Combustion DNS: A Compressible 2-D Shear Layer DNS Solver for TCR Model Validation

content: The TCR Micro-Mixing Model The TCR (Turbulence-Chemistry Recursive) model addresses a fundamental issue in transported PDF methods: traditional models (IEM, EMST) require empirical calibration for the mixing frequency. TCR eliminates this by using a recursive multi-layer partitioned reactor concept: $$\kappa = \frac{\tilde{\omega}_c}{\omega_c(\tilde{\phi})}$$ where: $\kappa$ = PSR volume fraction (mixing mode parameter) $\tilde{\omega}_c$ = DNS-averaged chemical source term $\omega_c(\tilde{\phi})$ = chemical source term evaluated at the mean composition The DNS provides the ground truth to evaluate this closure and its sensitivity to local mixing conditions.
title: ShearLayer-Combustion DNS: A Compressible 2-D Shear Layer DNS Solver for TCR Model Validation

content: 2. Governing Equations
title: ShearLayer-Combustion DNS: A Compressible 2-D Shear Layer DNS Solver for TCR Model Validation

content: Compressible Navier-Stokes (2-D) The solver evolves the 2-D compressible Navier-Stokes equations in conservative form: $$ \frac{\partial \mathbf{U}}{\partial t} \frac{\partial \mathbf{F}_x}{\partial x} \frac{\partial \mathbf{F}y}{\partial y} = \mathbf{S}{\text{visc}} + \mathbf{S}_{\text{reac}} $$ The conservative state vector is: $$\mathbf{U} = [\rho,; \rho u,; \rho v,; \rho E,; \rho Z,; \rho Y,; \rho Z^2]^T$$ where: Symbol Meaning $\rho$ Density $u, v$ Streamwise and cross-stream velocity $E$ Total energy per unit mass $Z$ Mixture fraction (passive scalar) $Y$ Reaction progress variable $Z^2$ Mixture fraction variance
title: ShearLayer-Combustion DNS: A Compressible 2-D Shear Layer DNS Solver for TCR Model Validation

content: Inviscid Flux: Rusanov with WENO The inviscid fluxes are computed using the Rusanov (local Lax–Friedrichs) scheme: $$\mathbf{F} = \frac{1}{2}\left[ \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{U}^-) + \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{U}^+) - \lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{U}^+ - \mathbf{U}^-) \right]$$ where $\mathbf{U}^\pm$ are the reconstructed left and right states using 5th-order WENO (Jiang-Shu or Z variants).
title: ShearLayer-Combustion DNS: A Compressible 2-D Shear Layer DNS Solver for TCR Model Validation

content: Viscous Fluxes Second-order central differences for viscous momentum and energy fluxes, coupled with Sutherland’s law for molecular viscosity: $$\mu(T) = \mu_0 \left( \frac{T}{T_0} \right)^{3/2} \frac{T_0 + S}{T + S}$$
title: ShearLayer-Combustion DNS: A Compressible 2-D Shear Layer DNS Solver for TCR Model Validation

content: Reaction Model The H₂/O₂ chemistry uses a simplified Arrhenius mechanism: $$\dot{\omega}Y = k_r \left[ Y{\text{H}2}^a Y{\text{O}2}^b - \frac{Y}{k{\text{eq}}} \right] \exp\left(-\frac{E_a}{RT}\right)$$ where $Y_{\text{H}2}$ and $Y{\text{O}_2}$ are derived from $Z$ and $Y$ using the mixture fraction definition.

content: Shear Layer Initial Condition The velocity profile is a hyperbolic tangent: $$u(y) = u_1 + \frac{u_2 - u_1}{2} \left[ 1 + \tanh\left( \frac{y}{2\delta_\omega} \right) \right]$$ with localized sinusoidal or random perturbations to seed KH instability: $$v’(x, y, t=0) = A_0 \sin\left( \frac{2\pi x}{\lambda} \right) \exp\left( -\frac{y^2}{2\sigma^2} \right)$$

content: COmbustor Adaptive Simulation Toolkit Combustor Adaptive Simulation Toolkit User Manual This manual was translated using AI based on the Chinese version, some expressions may not be accurate. This manual introduces the use of COmbustor Adaptive Simulation Toolkit (COAST). The first half mainly talks about how to install, modify calculation examples, run calculations and view results through the SSH command line of the packaged version of the portable program; the second half introduces the unpackaged version of the complete workspace, mesh/restart/local refinement methods, and development and maintenance processes. The graphical auxiliary interface is a separate auxiliary facility and is generally not used as the main line of operation. This document is generated by integrating the chapter drafts under docs/manual_sections/; if you want to significantly modify a chapter in the future, it is recommended to modify the corresponding chapter draft first and then re-integrate it.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Page 1: Package environment configuration and coast-assistant The package version is suitable for users who “get a pre-packaged running package and then run the calculation example on the Linux server”. Common directory names are similar to: coast-runtime-<version>-linux-x86_64/ Packaged versions usually come with solvers, coastctl, coast_remap, template studies, documentation, WebUI and nanobot runtime assets. In the new environment, first confirm that the server is Linux x86_64 and that python3 and mpirun can be found: which python3 which mpirun After decompression, enter the package root directory. If you choose to run it in place, you can directly use the tools in the package: cd coast-runtime-<version>-linux-x86_64 bin/coast-assistant --self-test --require-runtime --json bin/coast-assistant --configure-model bin/coast-assistant If you choose to install to a fixed location, you can run: ./install.sh /opt/coast/runtime source /opt/coast/runtime/env/coast-env.sh coast-assistant bin/coast-assistant is the novice entrance to the packaged version. It is not the solver itself, but an assistant launcher: it will call the COAST MCP tool in the package to help you check the calculation example, read and modify the input file, view the mesh and boundary, do pre-run checks, start controlled short runs, monitor screen and run logs. When you need a browser interface, you can ask the assistant to open the WebUI; the left side of the WebUI is chat, and the right side is the file and run workbench. In the packaged version, if you start the real solver through assistant/nanobot, you still have to follow the safety process: preflight first, then confirm startup, and then monitor the process, screen and monitor. Do not let the assistant use ordinary shell commands to bypass the controlled process to start the solver; if you do not use the assistant, please follow the ordinary manual commands in the running chapter of this manual. If you encounter other problems, such as “how to change the inlet temperature”, “why preflight does not pass”, “what does this error in the screen mean”, “how to download the Visit results”, you can directly ask coast-assistant and let it check with the tools in the project before giving suggestions.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Page 2: Source version environment configuration and coast-assistant The source code version is suitable for users who need to recompile, modify source code, synchronize compilableCode, debug tools or prepare new packages. Common directories are full workspaces or compilable source trees, for example: Coast_software/ compilableCode/ The source code version does not work by just copying an executable file. It needs to retain SRC.Coast/, EXEC/, docs/, scripts/, third_party/ and tool entries in the root directory. In the new environment, first check the compilation and running dependencies: which python3 which make which g++ which mpif90 which mpicxx which mpirun After entering the root directory of the source code version, first do a layout check: cd compilableCode chmod +x coastctl coast-ui coast-assistant scripts/*.sh ./scripts/check_layout.sh ./scripts/print_quickstart.sh When recompiling is required, execute under SRC.Coast: cd SRC.Coast make clean make -j"$(nproc)" cd .. After successful compilation, the main products are: EXEC/coast EXEC/coast_remap The source version of ./coast-assistant is not a binary compiled by make, but a startup script that comes with the source tree. It will call SRC.Coast/tools/coast_assistant.py and the tools in the same directory. Run on first use: ./coast-assistant --self-test --json ./coast-assistant --configure-model ./coast-assistant In the source code version, the manual entry for ordinary users is still: cd EXEC mpirun -np N ./coast When nanobot/assistant starts the solver, you must run coast_run_preflight, then coast_run_short(confirm=true), and monitor the process, screen and monitor after starting. In the source code version, if you encounter problems such as compilation failure, missing dependencies, unknown configuration of EXEC, unclear mesh/restart status, which tests should be run, whether it can be packaged, etc., you can also ask ./coast-assistant first. It will prioritize reading the project description and controlled tool output before telling you what to do next. 0. Introduction to the manual Welcome to COAST. This manual is written for users who are new to COAST. By default, readers do not need to have a programming foundation, nor do they need to learn computational fluids, combustion, parallel computing or Linux system management. All you need to know is that you need to log into the Linux server via SSH, prepare a calculation, check the settings, run the calculation from the command line, and view the results. This part is responsible for the first introductory content, mainly talking about the package version, that is, how to use the portable running package. If you get a packaged coast-runtime-<version>-linux-x86_64 directory, you can start here.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 0.1 Who is this manual for? This manual is suitable for the following users: I want to run COAST first and understand the process from preparation, running to viewing results; You need to operate COAST on the Linux server through the SSH command line on a Windows computer; Don’t want to touch the source code, compilation, test scripts and development directories from the beginning; Want to know what the words EXEC_TEMPLATE, *.d, Restart, Visit, and port forwarding mean; In the future, you may modify boundary conditions, run calculations, and export results, but now you need to complete the first time getting started. Note: This is not a developer source code description. You don’t need to understand the technical details of Fortran, MPI, turbulence models, and combustion mechanisms. The most important thing for novices is to distinguish “which files can be copied and modified, and which directories cannot be deleted casually.”
title: COAST User Manual

content: 0.2 Which path is recommended for novices to take first? Newbies are recommended to use the encapsulated version of the SSH command line path: Use SSH to log in to the Linux server on the Windows side. Unzip the COAST portable package on the Linux server. Copy EXEC_TEMPLATE to create your own working study. Use a text editor or command line tool to modify the *.d settings file. Use the command line to inspect the study, boundaries, and mesh. Use coastctl run --preflight to do a pre-start check, and then use coastctl run --execute to start the calculation. Use coastctl monitor, screen, external .coast_run_logs/ log and Visit/ to view the running status and results. If you really need graphical preview, start the graphical auxiliary interface separately; it is not the main line running mode. The advantage of this path is that you don’t need to compile the program or install a complete development environment on your local machine. The portable package already contains the coast-solver executable program, command line helpers, clean study templates and necessary documentation required to run it. The carrying case also offers the nanobot assistant as an optional newbie assistant. Run in browser mode bin/coast-nanobot-webui --package-root ., the left side is the dialogue and the right side is COAST Workbench for uploading, file viewing/editing/downloading, pre-run checks, sprinting, monitoring, stopping and logging tail; run bin/coast-nanobot-chat --package-root . in terminal mode. assistant should only pass COAST MCP tool operation must pass preflight before actual operation, and requires explicit confirmation.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 0.3 What is the difference between the encapsulated version and the unencapsulated version? COAST has two common forms: encapsulated version and unencapsulated version. They are two program forms for different purposes: the packaged version is used for daily running calculation examples, and the unpackaged version is used for source code development, compilation, testing and maintenance.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 0.3.1 What is the packaged version? The packaged version is also called a portable runtime package, which is usually a directory like this: coast-runtime-<version>-linux-x86_64/ SKILL.md bin/coast-solver bin/coast_remap bin/coastctl bin/coast-ui bin/coast-mcp bin/coast-standard-test bin/coast-nanobot-chat bin/coast-nanobot-webui env/coast-env.sh EXEC_TEMPLATE/ ui/static/ docs/USER_MANUAL.md docs/COAST_NANOBOT_ASSISTANT.md nanobot/ agent_skills/ manifest.json PACKAGE_AUDIT.json install.sh The packaged version can be understood as a “organized running toolbox”. It contains: bin/coast-solver: COAST’s solver ontology, the program that actually performs calculations; bin/coast_remap: C++ Restart remapping backend, coastctl run is used by default when the old Restart needs to be prepared to the new runtime mesh; bin/coastctl: command line operation tool, used to check calculation examples, view grid status, start running, monitor and stop; bin/coast-ui: Optional graphical auxiliary interface backend, generally not used as the mainline running mode; bin/coast-nanobot-webui and bin/coast-nanobot-chat: optional nanobot assistant entrance, respectively used for browser left chat/right workbench and terminal dialogue; bin/coast-mcp and bin/coast-standard-test: used by assistant and standard checks controlled tool access; env/coast-env.sh: environment setting script, used to tell the current terminal where to find the COAST tool; EXEC_TEMPLATE/: clean calculation example template, which should be copied before use; docs/: documentation; agent_skills/: Operation instructions for automated assistants. Packaged versions usually do not contain complete source code, development and test directories, large Restart data or large Visit results. Ordinary users do not need these contents when running calculation examples daily.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 0.3.2 What is the unpackaged version? The unpackaged version is a complete development workspace, usually similar to: Coast_software/ SKILL.md docs/ scripts/ tests/ SRC.Coast/ EXEC/ The unpackaged version includes source code, tests, tool scripts and default development examples. It is suitable for developers, maintainers or users who need to recompile COAST. For example: Modify the COAST program source code; Rebuild the development moderator executable program; Run development tests; Package new packaged version; Debug grid, restart, parallel exchange and other low-level methods. Note: If you just want to run existing calculation examples, modify input files, and view results, it is not recommended to start directly from the unpackaged version at the novice stage. The unpackaged version can do more and is more likely to accidentally delete or modify key files.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 0.3.3 How to choose between the two If you get the package package and the goal is to “run the calculation example”, please use the package version. If you need to modify the program source code, recompile COAST, or someone explicitly asks you to work in SRC.Coast, tests, scripts, then use the unpackaged version. A simple way to judge: What do you want to do Recommended use Trial COAST for the first time Packaged version Create your own working study Packaged version Edit study settings using browser Packaged version Check bounds and mesh Packaged version Start calculation with a limited number of steps Packaged version View Visit output Packaged version Modify COAST source code Unpackaged version Recompile the program Unpackaged version Package new runtime package Unpackaged version
title: COAST User Manual

content: 0.4 Safety principles to remember when reading this manual First, don’t modify EXEC_TEMPLATE directly. It is a clean template and should be left as is. Every time you do a demonstration, test or formal calculation, first copy a working example, such as EXEC.demo, EXEC.my_case. Second, do not delete these directories in user calculations: Restart/ runtime_mesh/ Decomp/ Geometry/ Visit/ These directories may hold restart data, running grids, parallel partitions, geometry files, and results files. After deletion, some calculations may not be continued and some results may not be opened again. Third, don’t start long-term formal calculations right away. It is recommended to do a short step test first to confirm that the calculation example can be started normally, that there are no obvious errors in the boundaries, and that the output directory is normal before doing the formal calculation. Fourth, when a Windows browser accesses the COAST graphical interface on a Linux server, SSH port forwarding is usually required. The browser address looks like 127.0.0.1, but the real program is running on a Linux server.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 0.5 Quick check on common terms
title: COAST User Manual

content: COAST COAST is the name of the calculation program. It is responsible for reading the study setup, mesh, boundary conditions and initial data, and then performing numerical calculations of flow, combustion or related physical processes. In the encapsulated version, the program that actually performs the calculation is usually: bin/coast-solver
title: COAST User Manual

content: Calculation example A calculation example is a “folder of a calculation task”. It contains the input files, grid information, boundary conditions, restart data and output results required for this calculation. EXEC_TEMPLATE in the package version is a template calculation example. You should copy it to get your own working example, for example: EXEC.demo/ EXEC.engine_test/ EXEC.case001/
title: COAST User Manual

content: Grid A grid is a way of dividing the computational space into many small grids. COAST does not directly calculate in continuous space, but gradually calculates velocity, pressure, temperature, components and other quantities on these small grids. The grid can be understood as “graph paper for calculations”. The finer the grid, the better it can describe complex structures, but the amount of calculation is also greater.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Boundary Boundaries are the outer shell or internal solid surfaces of the calculation area. Common boundaries include entrances, exits, and walls. Inlet: the fluid enters the calculation area from here; Exit: where the fluid leaves the calculation area; Wall: a solid surface that fluid cannot pass through; IBM Surfaces: Complex geometric surfaces identified by the immersed boundary method. Boundary conditions tell COAST: “What physical state should be on this boundary.” For example, what is the inlet velocity, what is the temperature, how to handle the outlet pressure, and whether there is no slip on the wall.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Restart Restart is the restart data directory. It saves the calculation state at a certain moment so that COAST can continue calculation from this state instead of starting from scratch every time. You can think of Restart as a game save. If there is no archive, you can only start from the initial state; if there is an archive, you can continue from the middle. Note: Restart files are usually related to the number of ranks for parallel calculations. The direct command for ordinary users is still cd EXEC && mpirun -np N ./coast. If MPI size differs from the active runtime mesh rank count, and input.d and Mesh-5 configuration allow startup regrid / restart remap, the startup phase will take the controlled preflight/write/remap path before solver reads fields and write brief diagnostics to screen. If the rank, Restart file, mesh identity, remap backend, or gate conditions are not met, startup will fail and close with diagnostics retained, rather than semi-automatically entering solution.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Visit Visit is the results output directory, also often refers to a set of result files used by VisIt visualization software. COAST typically generates: Visit/solution.visit Visit/solution.<step>.domain.<rank>.vtk Among them, solution.visit is like a directory list, which references many .vtk chunked result files. Simply copying solution.visit is usually not enough, the .vtk file it references must be brought along. Note: The Visit directory here is related to the name of the VisIt software. The term Visit is retained in the manual.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Server A server usually refers to a Linux machine running COAST. It might be a remote high-performance computing node, a workstation, or a Linux host in the lab. COAST calculations are typically run on Linux servers because they are computationally intensive, dependent on the Linux environment, and may require multiple CPU cores or MPI parallelism.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Graphical auxiliary interface The graphical auxiliary interface is a browser interface. The packaged version of COAST provides a Chinese graphical auxiliary interface, which allows you to check the status of calculation examples, modify commonly used *.d files, preview boundaries and grids, monitor operations, and organize Visit output without having to memorize many commands directly. The GUI backend is launched on a Linux server and Windows users access it via a browser.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Port The port is the house number of the network service. COAST GUI The default example uses the 18765 port. If the graphical auxiliary interface is started at 127.0.0.1:18765 of the server, it means: there is a web service on the 18765 port of the server that only allows local access.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Port forwarding Port forwarding is a “secure channel” provided by SSH. It can connect a local port on a Windows computer to a port on a Linux server. For example: ssh -N -L 18765:127.0.0.1:18765 user@server This means: When 127.0.0.1:18765 is opened on the Windows machine, SSH will forward the access to 127.0.0.1:18765 on the server. This is why the browser enters the local address, but what is seen is the COAST graphical interface page on the server. 1. First time meeting COAST This chapter explains the basic workings of COAST in a way that does not rely on professional background. You don’t need to memorize all the terms right away, just know what each thing is responsible for.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 1.1 What COAST does in a calculation A COAST calculation can be roughly thought of as the following process: Read case files -> Read or generate the mesh -> Identify boundaries and geometry -> Read the initial state or Restart -> Advance the calculation by time step -> Periodically write Restart and Visit results That said, COAST requires several key inputs: Calculation example settings: how long should be calculated this time, what is the output frequency, and which physical models should be used; Grid: How the calculation area is cut into small grids; Boundary conditions: How to deal with entrance, exit and wall respectively; Initial state: starting from scratch or continuing from a Restart archive; Running resources: How many ranks to use for parallel computing. During the calculation, COAST will write the result: screen or related logs: text information during runtime; Restart/: archive that can continue calculation; Visit/: Visualized results; Other diagnostic files: e.g. probe, heat release or statistical output.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 1.2 What is a calculation example? A study is a complete working folder. You can think of it as a project folder that contains everything needed for this calculation. There is a template in the package version: EXEC_TEMPLATE/ You should not run formal calculations directly on the template, but make a copy: EXEC.demo/ The copied EXEC.demo is your working example. Your subsequent editing of input.d, boundary_conditions.d, starting calculations, and generating results all occur in this working example. A typical working example might look like this: EXEC.demo/ input.d ibm_mesh.d boundary_conditions.d vtk_output.d spray.d spark.d probe.d heat_release.d Geometry/ Decomp/ Restart/ runtime_mesh/ Visit/ screen Not every study example starts with all directories. Some directories appear after generating a mesh, starting a calculation, or writing out results.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 1.3 What are *.d files? Many of COAST’s input settings are placed in text files ending with .d, for example: Documentation Main Purpose input.d Controls restart, total steps, output intervals, combustion and common solver settings ibm_mesh.d Controls geometry, mesh, IBM scan and static mesh related settings boundary_conditions.d Set up inlets, outlets, walls, coordinate selectors and components vtk_output.d Set which result fields Visit/VTK outputs spray.d Spray and evaporation related settings spark.d Ignition source related settings probe.d Pressure probe related settings heat_release.d Heat release diagnosis related settings These files are normal text files and can be opened with an editor. The packaged version of the graphical auxiliary interface will make some of the commonly used settings into forms, reducing the chance of manual editing errors. Note: Being able to open it does not mean that you can change it at will. At the novice stage, it is recommended to first modify common items through the graphical auxiliary interface, or strictly follow the instructions in subsequent chapters.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 1.4 Why is the grid important? COAST calculates the change of fluid in space and time. Computers cannot directly process infinite continuous space, so the area must first be cut into many small units, and these small units are grids. Grids affect: Calculate whether geometric shapes can be recognized; Are the entrances, exits and walls located correctly? Whether the results are detailed enough; Computing speed and memory usage; Whether Restart can continue to be used. If the mesh is too coarse, small structures may not be visible. If the grid is too fine, calculations can be very slow. For novices, there is no need to design complex grids by themselves when getting started for the first time. It is more important to learn to view the grid status and preview the boundaries first.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 1.5 Why are boundaries important? Boundary conditions tell COAST how the calculation area is connected to the outside world. Even if the mesh is correct and the boundary conditions are written incorrectly, the calculation may fail or result in physically meaningless results. Common examples: The direction of the inlet velocity is reversed, and the fluid may flow in from the outlet direction; The outlet is not set correctly and the pressure wave may be reflected; Wall leakage, fluid may pass through areas that should be solid; If the component name is written incorrectly, the corresponding species may not be found in the combustion calculation. The packaged version supports setting boundaries through boundary_conditions.d. It also supports coordinate selection boundaries, that is, using spatial ranges to specify which outer boundary grids belong to entrances, exits, or walls. This way common boundaries can be set even without the patch STL tag.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 1.6 Why Restart is like “Archive” Long calculations are not suitable for starting from scratch every time. COAST will write the status at certain times to the Restart/ directory, and you can continue from there next time. Restart usually includes data corresponding to each parallel rank. Rank can first be understood as “the number of jobs divided during parallel computing”. If an example is run with 128 ranks, COAST may divide the data into 128 parts. This is why special attention should be paid to the rank number when continuing the calculation. When the number of ranks, grids, and restart files do not match, COAST may fail to start. Note: Do not delete Restart/ just because it is large. Before deleting, you must confirm that renewal is no longer needed or that a backup has been saved.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 1.7 Why can’t Visit result send only one file? COAST’s Visit output is generally not a single result file, but a set of files. Common structures are: Visit/ solution.visit solution.000010.domain.000000.vtk solution.000010.domain.000001.vtk solution.000010.domain.000002.vtk ... solution.visit is like a directory listing, telling the VisIt software which .vtk files correspond to each time step. The real bulk of the data is in the .vtk files. So when sharing results, you can’t just send: Visit/solution.visit The .vtk file it references also needs to be sent along. Otherwise, others may only see empty results or report errors when they open it.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 1.8 Why Linux server and Windows side connections are usually needed Many users’ daily computers are Windows, and the COAST operating environment is usually on a Linux server. This is because: COAST has a large amount of calculation and is suitable for running on a server or workstation; Parallel computing, MPI, running scripts and file permissions are more common on Linux; Servers may have more CPU cores, more memory, and a more stable long-running environment. But users don’t have to sit in front of the server. Common working methods are: Windows computer Open the graphical assistant interface in a browser Set up SSH port forwarding in PowerShell | | Secure connection v Linux server Unpack the COAST portable package Store case files Start coast-ui Run the COAST calculation The effect of this is: the calculation remains on the server, and the operation interface is displayed in the Windows browser.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 1.9 Common directory structure diagram Assume that you place the package package in a fixed directory of the Linux server. The directory may look like this: /opt/coast/coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64/ bin/ coast-solver coast_remap coastctl coast-ui env/ coast-env.sh EXEC_TEMPLATE/ input.d ibm_mesh.d boundary_conditions.d vtk_output.d EXEC.demo/ input.d ibm_mesh.d boundary_conditions.d vtk_output.d Restart/ Visit/ docs/ USER_MANUAL.md Among them: coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64/ is the package root directory; EXEC_TEMPLATE/ is a template, do not change it directly; EXEC.demo/ is a copied working example, which can be modified according to tasks; bin/ contains running tools; env/ contains environment scripts; docs/ contains documentation. 2. Get started quickly with the packaged version This chapter walks through the first-time use process of the packaged version from the perspective of a new user. The command explains where to execute it and what you should see after execution. For convenience of explanation, the following assumptions are made: The Linux server username is user; The Linux server address is server; The COAST portable package file name is similar to coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64.tar.gz; The unzipped directory is called coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64; The working example is called EXEC.demo; Graphical auxiliary interface uses port 18765. In actual use, please replace user, server, version number and path with your real information.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.1 Prepare Linux server terminal First log in to the Linux server. You can use Windows PowerShell: ssh user@server This command is executed in Windows PowerShell. user is the server username, server is the server address, which can be a hostname or IP address. After execution, if this is the first time connecting, PowerShell may ask whether to trust the server fingerprint. After confirming that the address is correct, enter yes. Then enter the server password or use the key to log in. After successful login, you will see the Linux command prompt. Subsequent decompression and graphical auxiliary interface commands will be executed in this Linux terminal.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.2 Upload or find the COAST carrying bag If the administrator has placed the portable package on the server, you only need to change into the directory where it is located. If the portable package is on a Windows machine, you can use scp to upload it. This command is executed in Windows PowerShell: scp .\coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64.tar.gz user@server:~ The meaning is: Upload the compressed package in the current Windows directory to the server user’s home directory. After successful execution, there will generally not be a long output. You can check if the file exists after logging into the server: ls -lh ~/coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64.tar.gz This command is executed in the Linux server terminal. Normally, you will see the file size and file name.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.3 Unzip the portable bag In the Linux server terminal, enter the directory where you want to put COAST, such as your home directory: cd ~ Unzip the compressed package: tar -xzf coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64.tar.gz After execution, a directory will be generated: coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64/ Enter this directory: cd coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64 Check if there are key files inside: ls Under normal circumstances, you should see something like: SKILL.md bin docs env EXEC_TEMPLATE install.sh manifest.json If you don’t see bin, env, EXEC_TEMPLATE, it means you may not have entered the correct directory, or the compressed package is incomplete.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.4 Choose to install or run in place There are two ways to use the packaged version: install it in a fixed directory, or run it in place in the unzipped directory.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.4.1 Run in place If you are a novice trying it out for the first time, it is recommended to run it in place first. This will not copy the file elsewhere, and the path relationship is the most intuitive. Execute in the package root directory: source env/coast-env.sh This command will set the current terminal environment. There is usually no output if the execution is successful. Then check if coastctl is available: bin/coastctl doctor --case-dir EXEC_TEMPLATE --json Under normal circumstances, a JSON text containing the inspection results will be output. If you see obvious error, missing or the path does not exist, you need to first confirm whether the portable package is complete. Note: source env/coast-env.sh only takes effect on the current terminal. After reopening a Linux terminal, you need to execute it again.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.4.2 Install to fixed directory If you want to install COAST to a fixed location, such as $HOME/.local/coast, you can execute: bash install.sh "$HOME/.local/coast" This command is executed in the package root directory. It will install the runtime package to $HOME/.local/coast. After installation, before entering any directory, first load the environment script of the installation location: source "$HOME/.local/coast/env/coast-env.sh" Check if the installation is available: coastctl doctor --case-dir "$HOME/.local/coast/EXEC_TEMPLATE" --json The advantage of the installation method is that the path is stable; the advantage of running in situ is that it is simple and direct. When first learning, both are fine, but don’t mix multiple package versions on the same study.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.5 Create your own working study Do not modify EXEC_TEMPLATE directly. First make a copy of the working study. If you use run-in-place and are currently in the package root directory, execute: cp -a EXEC_TEMPLATE EXEC.demo cp -a will try to preserve directory structure and file attributes. There is usually no output if the execution is successful. Check whether the work study appears: ls EXEC.demo Under normal circumstances, you will see input files such as input.d, ibm_mesh.d, boundary_conditions.d, etc. Then verify the calculation example: bin/coastctl case validate --case-dir EXEC.demo --json This command will check whether the calculation input file is basically complete. Under normal circumstances, there should be no serious errors in the JSON output. Check the grid status again: bin/coastctl mesh status --case-dir EXEC.demo --json This command will check the current mesh-related status of the study. The output content of different calculation examples may be different, but if a key grid file is missing or the configuration is incorrect, it will usually be prompted here. If you use the installation method, the command may need to use the installed coastctl: coastctl case validate --case-dir "$HOME/.local/coast/EXEC.demo" --json Note: A separate working study directory is recommended for each demonstration, test or formal task. Don’t mix multiple tasks in the same EXEC.demo.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.6 Optional auxiliary: start the Chinese graphical auxiliary interface Graphical assistant interface is launched on the Linux server. Assuming that you are running in place and are currently in the package root directory, first confirm that the environment has been loaded: source env/coast-env.sh Then start the graphical assistant interface: bin/coast-ui --workspace "$PWD" --case-dir "$PWD/EXEC.demo" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18765 This command means: --workspace "$PWD": The current package directory is used as the workspace; --case-dir "$PWD/EXEC.demo": Use the working example just copied; --host 127.0.0.1: Only allow the server to access this Web service locally; --port 18765: Graphical auxiliary interface listens to port 18765. After execution, this Linux terminal will be occupied by the graphical auxiliary interface and will not return to the command prompt immediately. Under normal circumstances, you will see text related to service startup, indicating that the graphical auxiliary interface is running. Note: Do not close this terminal. After closing, the graphical auxiliary interface service will also stop. You can open another terminal to perform other operations. If you use the installation method, you can execute it similarly: coast-ui --workspace "$HOME/.local/coast" --case-dir "$HOME/.local/coast/EXEC.demo" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18765
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.7 Optional Assist: Setting up SSH port forwarding on Windows If the COAST GUI is launched on a remote Linux server, Windows browsers generally cannot directly access the server’s 127.0.0.1:18765. Because the server’s 127.0.0.1 refers to the server itself, not your Windows computer. At this time, you need to open a new window in Windows PowerShell and execute: ssh -N -L 18765:127.0.0.1:18765 user@server Please replace user@server with your server username and address. The meanings of several parts of this command are as follows: ssh: connect to the server; -N: Only establish a connection and do not open the remote command line; -L 18765:127.0.0.1:18765: Forward the 18765 port of the Windows machine to the 18765 port of the server machine; user@server: your server login information. After a successful execution, the PowerShell window usually stays there with no apparent output. This is normal. As long as this window remains open, port forwarding remains in effect. Note: Do not close this PowerShell window. After closing, the channel from the browser to the server graphical auxiliary interface will also be disconnected.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.8 Optional assistance: access the graphical assistance interface in the browser Keep both windows open: Linux server terminal: running bin/coast-ui...; Windows PowerShell: Running ssh -N -L .... Then enter in the Windows browser address bar: http://127.0.0.1:18765 Under normal circumstances, you will see the COAST Chinese graphical auxiliary interface page. Note: 127.0.0.1 here is the Windows native address. Due to SSH port forwarding, it is forwarded to the COAST graphical assistant on the Linux server.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.9 What to do if the local port 18765 is occupied If PowerShell prompts that the local port is already occupied, you can change it to a Windows local port, such as 18766: ssh -N -L 18766:127.0.0.1:18765 user@server This means: Windows natively uses 18766; Linux server GUI still uses 18765. To open in browser: http://127.0.0.1:18766 Note: Only the local port after the colon has changed, and the port of the server-side graphical auxiliary interface has not changed.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.10 Optional auxiliary: What can the graphical interface page do? Page names may vary slightly between versions of the COAST graphical assistance interface, but are generally organized around the following purposes.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.10.1 Calculation status The study status page is used to check which workspace and study directory are currently connected, and whether the input file is complete. You can confirm it here: Is the current calculation example EXEC.demo, not EXEC_TEMPLATE; Whether the key *.d files exist; Restart, Visit, whether the grid directory exists; Check whether there are any error messages in the latest check. If the page shows that the current calculation example is EXEC_TEMPLATE, you should stop the operation, return to the Linux terminal, copy a working calculation example, and then start the graphical interface.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.10.2 Input file form The input file form page is used to view and modify settings in common *.d files. Common uses include: Adjust the number of steps, output frequency, and restart switch in input.d; View mesh and geometry settings in ibm_mesh.d; Modify the output fields in vtk_output.d; Check the relevant settings of spray.d, spark.d, probe.d, heat_release.d. Newbies are advised to only change a small number of parameters at a time and verify them immediately after saving. Do not modify many files at once, otherwise it will be difficult to determine where an error occurred.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.10.3 Boundary conditions The Boundary Conditions page is used to view and edit boundary_conditions.d. You can confirm it here: Which areas are entrances; Which areas are exits; Which areas are walls; Boundary selection whether to use coordinate ranges or IBM surfaces; Whether the inlet velocity, temperature, pressure, and components are as expected. If the page provides a border preview function, it is recommended to preview it after each modification. Boundary conditions are one of the most common areas for beginners to make mistakes.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.10.4 Grid and IBM Preview The mesh and IBM preview pages are used to view the calculation area, mesh status, and identification of complex geometric surfaces. The goal here is not for novices to analyze all mesh details, but to identify the most basic issues: Whether the grid can be recognized; Whether the geometry is in the expected position; Whether the fluid region and the solid region are obviously reversed; Whether the boundary selection is empty; Check whether the grid status reports an error. If the preview appears empty, the range is clearly wrong, or the number of boundary selections is 0, it is not recommended to proceed with starting the formal calculation.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.10.5 Operation monitoring The run monitoring page is used to view whether COAST is running, as well as recent logs, step count, and output status. You can use it to determine: Whether the program started successfully; Which step is currently reached in calculation; -Whether Restart or Visit is written; Whether an error message appears; Whether the calculation needs to be stopped gracefully. Note: A short step test should be done before official operation. Do not just leave a new study running for a long time.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.10.6 Visit export and download The Visit output page is used to organize the visualization results. It usually helps you find: Visit/solution.visit; The corresponding .vtk chunked result file; Which time steps have been output; The set of files required to download or package the results. Again: solution.visit is not the complete result itself. When sharing results, they need to be processed along with the .vtk file it references.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.11 Common reasons and solutions for connection failures If the browser cannot open http://127.0.0.1:18765, do not rush to modify the calculation example. First check in the following order.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.11.1 The graphical auxiliary interface on the Linux server does not start Phenomenon: The browser prompts that it cannot be accessed; PowerShell port forwarding window looks normal; There is no coast-ui running on the Linux server. Processing method: Return to the Linux server terminal and restart in the package root directory: bin/coast-ui --workspace "$PWD" --case-dir "$PWD/EXEC.demo" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18765 Make sure the terminal does not exit immediately. If the command ends immediately and an error is displayed, first check the path and study directory according to the error prompt.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.11.2 SSH port forwarding is not established Phenomenon: The graphical auxiliary interface on the Linux server is running; Windows browser still cannot be opened; There is no running ssh -N -L ... window in PowerShell. Processing method: Re-execute in Windows PowerShell: ssh -N -L 18765:127.0.0.1:18765 user@server Keep this window open and refresh the browser.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.11.3 Incorrect user name, server address or login method Phenomenon: PowerShell prompts that the connection failed; Prompt for wrong password; Prompt that the host name cannot be resolved; Prompt for connection timeout. Processing method: First confirm whether normal SSH can log in: ssh user@server If normal SSH fails to log in, port forwarding will not succeed either. You need to confirm the username, server address, network, VPN, password or key configuration first.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.11.4 The local port is occupied Phenomenon: PowerShell prompts that local port binding failed; The error message may contain words such as bind, address already in use, etc. Processing method: Change a Windows local port, for example: ssh -N -L 18766:127.0.0.1:18765 user@server Then the browser accesses: http://127.0.0.1:18766
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.11.5 Graphical auxiliary interface port is written incorrectly Phenomenon: The Linux side uses a port when starting; Another port is used for Windows forwarding or browser access; The three ports are not connected. Processing method: Confirm three settings: Linux coast-ui port: --port 18765 PowerShell forwarding: -L 18765:127.0.0.1:18765 Browser address: http://127.0.0.1:18765 If you use the local alternative port 18766, this would be: Linux coast-ui port: --port 18765 PowerShell forwarding: -L 18766:127.0.0.1:18765 Browser address: http://127.0.0.1:18766
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.11.6 Graphical auxiliary interface is bound to the wrong address Newbies are recommended to bind the graphical auxiliary interface to: 127.0.0.1 That is, use it at startup: bin/coast-ui --workspace "$PWD" --case-dir "$PWD/EXEC.demo" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18765 In this way, the graphical auxiliary interface is only open on the server itself, and then securely forwarded to the Windows browser through SSH. If you change --host to another address, you may encounter server firewall, security policy or access scope problems. It is not recommended to make random changes at the novice stage.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.11.7 Wrong calculation path Phenomenon: The browser can open the page, but the calculation example reported on the page does not exist; What is displayed on the page is not the calculation example you want to operate; Linux terminal prompts that case-dir does not exist. Processing method: Confirm the current directory and study directory in the Linux server terminal: pwd ls -ld EXEC.demo If the current directory is not the package root directory, you can use the absolute path to start the graphical auxiliary interface: bin/coast-ui --workspace "/opt/coast/coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64" --case-dir "/opt/coast/coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64/EXEC.demo" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18765 Please replace the path with your real path.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.11.8 Mistaking templates for working examples Phenomenon: Graphical auxiliary interface page shows that EXEC_TEMPLATE is being operated; You have not copied EXEC.demo; After modification, it was found that the template had been changed. Processing method: Stop the graphical auxiliary interface and copy the template again: cp -a EXEC_TEMPLATE EXEC.demo Then start with a working study: bin/coast-ui --workspace "$PWD" --case-dir "$PWD/EXEC.demo" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18765 If EXEC_TEMPLATE has been changed, do not continue to do formal tasks on it. Please contact the administrator or get a clean template from the original package.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 2.12 Checklist after getting started for the first time After completing this chapter, you should have: Know the difference between packaged and unpackaged versions; Know the basic meaning of COAST, calculation example, grid, boundary, Restart, and Visit; Unpacked the COAST portable package on the Linux server; Know how to choose to run in place or install to a fixed directory; Copied your own working example from EXEC_TEMPLATE; Used coastctl to do basic calculation example checking; Launched the Chinese graphical auxiliary interface on the Linux server; Set up SSH port forwarding in Windows PowerShell; Opened the COAST graphical auxiliary interface in the browser; Prioritize checking GUI, SSH forwarding, ports and paths when connection failure is known. The next step is usually to learn how to modify the study settings and boundary conditions. Before continuing, please make sure you are operating on the copied working study and not EXEC_TEMPLATE. 3. Modify calculation example settings This chapter talks about “how to safely modify a COAST calculation example after it already exists.” If you use the package version, it is recommended to copy EXEC_TEMPLATE first to get your own working example, such as EXEC.demo. All subsequent examples will use this name. Note: Do not modify the template directory directly, nor treat running products such as Restart, runtime_mesh, Decomp, and Visit as configuration files to modify manually. The settings are mainly in several *.d files.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.1 What can be changed in a calculation example? A common working example looks roughly like this: EXEC.demo/ input.d ibm_mesh.d boundary_conditions.d vtk_output.d spray.d spark.d probe.d heat_release.d mesh5_auto_refine.d Geometry/ Fuels/ Restart/ Decomp/ runtime_mesh/ Visit/ The most suitable for ordinary users to modify here are the *.d files listed above. They are text configuration files read when COAST starts and runs, recording information such as “how to run this calculation”, “where the grid and geometry come from”, “what are the entrances and exits”, “what results are output” and other information. Generally do not change these directories manually: Restart/: Restart the data and save the last calculated flow field. If you delete it casually, the calculation may fail. Decomp/: Parallel chunking and compatible grid files. It is usually generated by mesh tools. runtime_mesh/: authoritative data of the runtime grid, related to restart and rank number. Visit/: Result output directory. This is suitable for viewing and archiving, not for changing settings. Geometry/ and Fuels/: Geometry and fuel/mechanism data can be used as input, but novices should not replace them casually without understanding the units, coordinates and mechanism names.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.2 What are *.d files? *.d files are a type of text input file used by COAST. The .d here is not a programming language, nor is it a program that must be double-clicked to open; it is just an extension that represents a direct input file such as “direct input”. You can think of it as “calculation instructions”. When COAST starts, it will read these files according to fixed rules: Some files are read line by line, and the position of the value is important. For example, many old-fashioned configurations in input.d have this style. Some files use a block structure, such as &output_control ... /, which is called a namelist, like a set of named options. boundary_conditions.d uses a patch structure that is closer to human readability to describe entrances, exits and walls. #, !, C----- Such lines are usually comments to explain the following content; comments are generally not treated as numerical values. For example input.d might have a line like this: 5000 /lstep 500 /stepsave : write restart file interval 500 /stepplot : write plot file interval means: 5000 is the total number of steps lstep; Write a restart every 500 steps; Write plot/Visit output every 500 steps. Note: The old-fashioned file read by line cannot add or delete lines or change the order at will. You can change the value at the beginning of the line, but don’t move the entire paragraph elsewhere.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.3 Do two things before modifying First, make sure you are changing the working example, not the template. The following command is executed in the package running directory, which is the directory where bin/coastctl and EXEC_TEMPLATE can be seen. cp -a EXEC_TEMPLATE EXEC.demo After execution, you should see an additional EXEC.demo directory. Subsequent modifications are made in EXEC.demo. Second, make a backup copy of individual files before changing them. For example, if you want to change input.d: cp -a EXEC.demo/input.d EXEC.demo/input.d.before_edit There should be one more EXEC.demo/input.d.before_edit after execution. If you make corrections, you can restore specific lines against this backup. Note: Do not use methods such as git reset, batch deletion, and clearing directories to “recover”. There may be other people working on other files in the same workspace.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.4 Graphical auxiliary interface What is the difference between modification and text modification? The COAST package version provides a Chinese graphical auxiliary interface and also allows you to modify *.d files directly with a text editor. The two methods modify the same batch of calculation example files, but are suitable for different scenarios. How What to do Advantages Risks Graphical auxiliary interface modification Novices can change common switches, view calculation case status, preview boundaries, check grids and outputs It is not easy to find wrong files; the interface will display some files together; suitable for modification while viewing The interface does not necessarily expose all advanced parameters; if multiple people modify the same calculation example at the same time, they may overwrite each other Text modification Accurately modify a certain line, copy the fragments given by others, and compare configurations in batches Complete, direct, and reviewable; suitable for use when there is a clear modification goal It is easy to miss semicolons, correct wrong units, and delete necessary lines, especially for old-fashioned sequential reading of files The recommended approach for newbies is: Use the graphical auxiliary interface to review the general settings first to confirm which calculation example you are operating. When you only need to change one or two items, you can change them in the graphical interface. When you need to paste the complete boundary patch and accurately adjust the coordinate range, you can use a text editor to change it. After changing the text, return to the graphical interface or use coastctl to check. Note: Do not open the same file in the browser, graphical interface, and text editor at the same time and save it repeatedly. Save one side first, then refresh the other side.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.5 Quick check on commonly used *.d files File Main purpose Frequently modified content for newbies Special reminder input.d Global run control, restart, total steps, output interval, burning/PDF switch, time step and debugging switch lstep, stepsave, stepplot, whether to restart, debugging output Line order is very important; do not change the physical model you do not understand ibm_mesh.d Geometry/STL, IBM immersion boundary, mesh generation, mesh resolution, parallel tiling, Mesh-4 preview Geometry file path, preview switch, target rank, mesh report Changing it may cause mesh, restart and rank mismatch boundary_conditions.d Inlet, outlet, wall, coordinate selection, patch/STL selection, velocity temperature and pressure components Inlet velocity, outlet pressure, wall temperature, methane/air component, coordinate range Chapter 4 of this chapter explains in detail; must be previewed after modification vtk_output.d Which variables are output by Visit/VTK Switch certain output fields and diagnostic levels The more output, the larger the file size spray.d Spray, droplets, evaporation, nozzle position and spray output Whether spray, spray fuel, nozzle parameters are enabled Gas phase combustion studies usually remain off spark.d Ignition source, ignition time, ignition position, ignition duration Ignition switch, ignition point coordinates, starting steps Ignition position must fall in a reasonable fluid area probe.d Control of monitoring points such as pressure probes Whether to enable, sampling interval The current file may be very short, the common format is switch plus interval heat_release.d Global heat release rate history or diagnostic data Usually not manually modified May be written at runtime; only processed when it is clearly necessary to continue the heat release history mesh5_auto_refine.d Mesh-5 automatic local refinement candidate scoring Whether to enable candidate generation and the weight of each score Candidate generation is not equal to formal replacement of the solution mesh Explain one by one below.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.6 input.d: running main switch input.d is the most important global control file. It does not describe the specific entrances and exits, but tells COAST how the calculation example runs as a whole. Common content includes: Whether to read old results from Restart/ and continue calculation. Whether to write a new Restart/ file. Total number of steps lstep. Write restart interval stepsave. Write interval stepplot for Visit/VTK results. Physical switches such as LES, combustion, reaction mechanism, PDF, compressible flow, etc. Time step limit, Mach number protection, debugging output and other running protection switches. The most common modification for beginners is to make the total number of steps smaller and do a short test first. For example it turned out to be: 5000 /lstep 500 /stepsave : write restart file interval 500 /stepplot : write plot file interval If you just want to run 50 steps first to see if it can start, you can change it to: 50 /lstep 25 /stepsave : write restart file interval 25 /stepplot : write plot file interval This means running up to 50 steps, writing a restart and result every 25 steps. After passing the short test, increase the number of steps. Regarding restarting, there is usually something like this in input.d: true true /restart, write to restart The first true means reading from an existing restart, and the second true means continuing to write restarts while running. Beginners should note: If there are no files matching the current rank number in Restart/, but read restart is set, the operation will fail. If you’re just starting from a clean template, you generally shouldn’t force read restarts that don’t exist. If you take a calculation example that has been run by others, make sure it can still be used after restarting before changing the rank number, grid or geometry. The second half of input.d also has blocks like this: &time_control time_step_cap_enabled = .true. time_step_max = 9.9e-06 time_step_growth_limit = 1.20 / Each line in this block has a name, making it easier to read. The above indicates that the maximum time step limit is enabled. The maximum time step is 9.9e-06 seconds, and the new time step increases by up to 20% each time. If the calculation is unstable at the beginning, you can ask an experienced person to look at these protection parameters first. It is not recommended for novices to significantly relax themselves.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.7 ibm_mesh.d: Geometry, Mesh, and IBM ibm_mesh.d Pipe geometry and mesh. IBM is the abbreviation of immersed boundary method, which can be understood as the method of “using STL/CAD geometry to mark solids, fluids and walls in the background grid”. Common blocks in this file include: &mesh_control: whether to start mesh generation, whether to write preview, whether to overwrite the old Decomp/. &mesh_runtime: Which mesh the current solver uses as authoritative. &mesh_regrid: Mesh-4 preview and candidate mesh related settings. The current safe path is usually only labeling and previewing, and does not directly move the solution grid. &ibm_control: Whether to enable IBM, main geometry file path, STL units, wall damping, etc. &mesh_geometry: Geometry file list, STL/CAD units, geometry expansion or contraction. &mesh_domain: Computational domain range, which can be automatically derived from geometry or given manually. &mesh_resolution: basic grid spacing and minimum grid spacing. &mesh_ibm: fluid/solid markers, interface layers, CAD openings, etc. &mesh_decomposition: target MPI rank number, blocking method, forced alignment coordinate plane. If you only change the inlet velocity, temperature, and outlet pressure in the existing calculation example, you generally do not need to touch ibm_mesh.d. If you replace the geometry file, change the mesh resolution, or change target_ranks, it may affect: Whether Decomp/ needs to be rebuilt; Whether Restart/ can still be used; Whether runtime_mesh/ matches the current calculation example; Boundary coordinate selection whether the original entrance and exit can still be selected. Note: boundary_conditions.d can only assign values ​​to existing boundary surfaces, and cannot “dig” solid areas in STL into entrances. If an internal nozzle does not have a fluid connection surface, you need to first create the opening through ibm_mesh.d and the mesh generation process, and then assign velocity and components in the boundary file.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.8 vtk_output.d: Control Visit/VTK output vtk_output.d determines which variables are written in the result file. The more Visit/VTK outputs, the easier post-processing is, but the file size is also larger. Common writing methods are: default true vtk_diag_level 1 01_Velocity true 02_Static_pressure true 02_Temperature true 04_Heat_release_rate true It can be understood like this: default true: Fields not listed in the file are output according to the program’s default behavior. default false: Only output fields explicitly written as true. vtk_diag_level: diagnostic level. The higher the level, the more diagnostic fields and the larger the file. Field name true: Output this field. Field name false: Turn off this field. Newbies are advised to leave default true and a lower diagnostic level. Reduce the output only when the disk space is obviously insufficient, or when someone clearly tells you that only certain fields are needed.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.9 spray.d: spray and droplets spray.d controls spray, droplets, evaporation, mass/momentum coupling between droplets and gases, and nozzle geometry. Gas phase methane/air combustion studies typically maintain: spray = .false. When spray = .true., the TCR_MULTI_INJECT block later in the file defines the number of nozzles, droplet diameter distribution, spray position, direction, cone angle, particle rate and spray velocity. Note: Spray is not as simple as “outputting a few more particle maps”, it will change the computational physics process. Do not open when spray is not required.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.10 spark.d: Spark settings spark.d controls the ignition model, such as whether to ignite, ignition duration, ignition start time, maximum ignition temperature, number of ignition points and ignition coordinates. Typical content might look like this: true ! spark: true or false 0.005 ! spark duration time used by qdot_max (s) 0.0 ! spark initiation time used by legacy time model (s) 295.0 1800.0 ! initial air temperature and maximum spark temperature (K) 4 ! number of sparks The following multiple lines of coordinates are the ignition point location, and the unit is usually meters. The ignition point should be located near a reasonable fluid area and flammable mixing area. If the ignition point falls inside a solid, outside a wall, or in an area with no fuel/oxidant at all, the calculation may run without ignition. NOTE: There may also be a master switch for “ignition enabled” in input.d. Whether to actually ignite or not requires the content of the main switch and spark.d to be reasonable together.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.11 probe.d: Probe settings probe.d is used for simple monitoring settings such as pressure probes. In some current calculations, it may only have two short terms, for example: false 10 It can be roughly understood as settings such as “whether to enable” and “sampling interval”. Ordinary users usually don’t need to modify it if they just look at the overall field diagram and logs.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.12 heat_release.d: Heat release rate history heat_release.d usually saves historical data of global heat release rate changes over time. A common form is two columns of numbers: the first column is like time, and the second column is like heat release rate or related diagnostic quantities. If an entry like the following in input.d is false: false /read global heat release rate: true/false Then heat_release.d is more of a diagnostic result written at runtime. Only if you explicitly want to append from the existing global heat release rate history and set this read switch to true will it be used as an existing history. Note: Do not treat heat_release.d as an ordinary parameter table and change it casually. Changing it will usually not help you “tune the combustion” but will make the historical diagnosis less credible.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.13 mesh5_auto_refine.d: Automatic local refinement candidates mesh5_auto_refine.d controls the scoring of Mesh-5 automatic partial refine candidates. It is not a switch to “immediately let the solver change the grid”. Instead, it uses indicators such as geometry, vorticity, reaction rate, etc. to score areas that may need to be refined and generate candidate packages or reports. Common content is similar to: enabled = false on_restart = false geometry_weight = 0.40 vorticity_weight = 0.30 reaction_weight = 0.30 top_fraction = 0.05 min_fluid_fraction = 0.02 means: enabled = false: Candidates are not automatically generated by default. geometry_weight: scoring weight close to the geometry/wall. vorticity_weight: vorticity related score weight. reaction_weight: reaction intensity related scoring weight. top_fraction: Select a part of the area with top scores. NOTE: Candidate ciphers are suggestions only and not an official production grid. To actually use the new grid for calculations, you still need to go through the restarting and remapping, pre-checking and rollback protection processes. Beginners should not regard it as a button to “make the results more accurate with one click”.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 3.14 How to check after modification Every time after modifying the *.d file, it is recommended to check it first before running it officially. The following command is executed in the package running directory, which is the directory where bin/coastctl can be seen. The first step is to check whether the calculation example configuration can be read: bin/coastctl case validate --case-dir EXEC.demo --json You should see a JSON output. Under normal circumstances, there should be no obvious errors such as error, failed, and missing. This check mainly finds missing files, format errors, and obviously illegal configurations.
