title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.8.1 Configuration issues Common manifestations: Missing input file; A certain *.d format is wrong; The output frequency is 0 or unreasonable; Restart switch and file do not match; Misspelling of species name; The path points to a file that does not exist. First run: bin/coastctl case validate --case-dir EXEC.demo --json bin/coastctl doctor --case-dir EXEC.demo --json If they report an error, fix the configuration first.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.8.2 Running environment issues Common manifestations: mpirun not found; -MPI error reporting; The program does not have permission to execute; The login node is not allowed to run for a long time; The disk is full; Insufficient memory; Repeated startup of the same calculation example directory. examine: which mpirun ls -l bin/coast-solver bin/coastctl monitor --case-dir EXEC.demo --json If it is a cluster resource problem, you usually need to contact the administrator or use the job scheduling system.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.8.3 Grid or IBM issues Common manifestations: The log mentions IBM, mesh, STL, and mask; The border preview is empty; Abnormal grid status; The mesh saved in Restart is inconsistent with the current runtime_mesh/; Geometry changed, but still using old Restart. examine: bin/coastctl mesh status --case-dir EXEC.demo --json bin/coastctl boundary preview --case-dir EXEC.demo --write --json If you have changed the geometry or mesh, do not directly use the old Restart unless you have done Restart remapping and preflight according to a special process.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.8.4 Numerical Divergence Common manifestations: NaN appears in screen or external stdout/stderr log; Inf or infinity appears; Residual error, speed, temperature, and pressure suddenly become extremely large; Program abort in advance; A large area of unreasonable color appears in the result image, and then the program fails. Numerical divergence may be caused by many reasons, such as too large a time step, unreasonable boundary conditions, too large a difference between the initial field and the boundary, poor mesh quality, incorrect physical property or component settings, too strong spray/combustion source terms, etc. Novices should not directly judge that “a certain model must be broken.” Collect first: bin/coastctl monitor --case-dir EXEC.demo --json tail -120 EXEC.demo/screen The actual files for stdout/stderr are read from the stdoutLog and stderrLog fields in the monitor output. Then record the step at which the failure occurred, which field was abnormal first, and which inputs were recently changed.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.8.5 Normal early stop Not all “stops” are failures. The following may be normal stops: reach lstep; The set end time is reached; User created stop_coast; The log appears finished; The log appears time > tlast or istep > lstep: stop; Write Restart and Visit before stopping. This is a good thing if the program runs the short test and stops as expected. Don’t think of “program exit” itself as an error.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.9 coastctl run prompts that it is already running and is active
title: COAST User Manual

content: Phenomenon The startup times are similar to: existing coast run appears active
title: COAST User Manual

content: Reason coastctl records the last time in the external state file of .coast_run_logs/_state/ Started process number and check that this process still exists. It will prevent you from doing this in the same study directory Repeated startup prevents two COASTs from writing the same batch of Restart/ and Visit/ at the same time.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Processing steps First monitor: bin/coastctl monitor --case-dir EXEC.demo --json If it is still running, do not start it again. If you need to stop, execute: bin/coastctl stop --case-dir EXEC.demo --json If you confirm that the previous process has ended but the record still exists, check the log and process status first. Then contact someone with experience to handle it. Do not delete the status file in .coast_run_logs/_state/ Restart immediately unless you confirm that no old process is still writing files.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.10 There are fatal, abort, NaN or Inf in the log
title: COAST User Manual

content: Phenomenon There is content in errorSummary of coastctl monitor, or the following appears in the log: fatal abort NaN Inf infinity
title: COAST User Manual

content: Processing steps The first step is to stop expanding losses. If the program is still running, stop it gently: bin/coastctl stop --case-dir EXEC.demo --json The second step is to save the scene. Do not delete screen, external stdout/stderr logs, Restart/ or Visit/. The third step is to collect logs: bin/coastctl monitor --case-dir EXEC.demo --json tail -120 EXEC.demo/screen The actual files for stdout/stderr are read from the stdoutLog and stderrLog fields in the monitor output. The fourth step is to recall recent changes: Whether the boundary conditions have been changed; Whether the inlet speed, temperature, pressure or composition has been changed; Whether the grid has been changed; Whether to continue calculation from the old Restart; Whether the rank number has been changed; Whether spray, ignition or combustion related settings are enabled; Whether the official step number and output interval were written incorrectly. Note: Results generated after NaN or Inf should generally not be used as official results. Even if VisIt can be opened, it can only be used for troubleshooting and should not be used to report conclusions.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.11 Restart/runtime_mesh is inconsistent with the current mesh
title: COAST User Manual

content: Phenomenon When resuming, the log or tool prompts that the mesh identity saved by Restart does not match the current runtime_mesh/, or mentions restart-to-new-mesh remap related information.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Reason Restart not only saves the digital field, but also is related to the current grid partition. COAST will now save the runtime mesh information corresponding to Restart to prevent you from hard-copying the old flow field to the new mesh. If you change geometry, regenerate meshes, or change tiles, the old Restart may no longer be suitable for direct reading.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Processing steps First check: bin/coastctl mesh status --case-dir EXEC.demo --json If you just want to continue the last calculation, you should not replace runtime_mesh/. Retrieve the runtime_mesh/ matched with Restart, or use the complete old calculation example directory to continue the calculation. If you do move from an old mesh to a new mesh, this is part of the Restart remapping or Mesh-4/Mesh-5 advanced process. Novices should not move files manually to complete this operation. They should use coastctl run --preflight to view the controlled plan, and then use coastctl run --execute to complete the production prepare/remap/activation. Ordinary users can still use cd EXEC && mpirun -np N ./coast in the manual path; if MPI size differs and startup regrid / restart remap is allowed, the startup phase will take the controlled preflight/write/remap path before the solver reads fields. If it fails, it will fail to close and retain the diagnosis. Common remap/preflight failure reasons include: missing coast_remap, inconsistent rank or number of files, failed marker transition gate, staging output directory already exists but overwrite is not allowed, or progress file is placed in output-dir.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.12 The graphical auxiliary interface can be opened, but the startup fails.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Phenomenon The browser can open the graphical interface, but it fails after clicking Run.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Common reasons The --case-dir pointed to by the graphical auxiliary interface is not the calculation example you want to run; The rank number is entered incorrectly; case validate failed; The server cannot find mpirun; The executable main solver cannot be found in the package directory; There is already a running COAST; The graphical auxiliary interface does not have permission to write the calculation example directory in the background; The Restart switch in input.d does not match the actual file.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Processing steps Return to the server terminal and execute the same command, and the error will be clearer: bin/coastctl doctor --case-dir EXEC.demo --json bin/coastctl run --case-dir EXEC.demo --ranks 128 --preflight --write --json If you can’t pass preflight, don’t click official start in the graphical interface yet.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.13 Graphical auxiliary interface post-processing failed
title: COAST User Manual

content: Phenomenon The graphical auxiliary interface can see the Visit data, but fails to generate images, prompting that VisIt cannot be found, or that a certain dataset, field, or plot type is not supported.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Common reasons VisIt is not installed on the server; visit command is not in PATH; COAST_VISIT_BIN is not set or points to an error; .visit exists but the corresponding .vtk is incomplete; The selected field does not exist in the data set; Vector plot selected, but without full velocity components; VisIt background operation times out or reports an error.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Processing steps Check VisIt: which visit If there is no output, install VisIt or set up: export COAST_VISIT_BIN=/path/to/visit Then restart the graphical assistant interface. Check Visit file integrity: find EXEC.demo/Visit -maxdepth 1 -name '*.visit' | wc -l find EXEC.demo/Visit -maxdepth 1 -name '*.vtk' | wc -l If the field selection fails, first change to a scalar field that clearly exists in the graphical assistant interface as Pseudocolor, such as temperature, pressure or mark field. After confirming that the basic cloud chart can be generated, try the contour or vector chart again.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.14 Insufficient disk space
title: COAST User Manual

content: Phenomenon The calculation fails during running, the Visit or Restart file is incomplete, the log may show that the file cannot be written, a file system error, or the server prompts quota exceeded.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Reason Both Visit/ and Restart/ can be large. When there are many ranks, high output frequency, and large number of steps, the number of files will increase rapidly.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Processing steps Check the study directory size: du -sh EXEC.demo du -sh EXEC.demo/Visit EXEC.demo/Restart If there is insufficient space, stop the calculation first, and then confirm with the person in charge which old results can be archived or deleted. Do not delete files being written while the program is running. Newbies can safely give priority to: Download and archive old Visit zips that are no longer needed for viewing online; Copy the complete calculation case and then clean the copy; Keep the most recent renewable complete Restart/. Note: Don’t just keep solution.visit to save space. It cannot recover results alone.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.15 When to stop and contact the developer If the following situation occurs, it is recommended to stop trying and contact the developer or administrator after sorting the logs: Repeated occurrences of NaN, Inf or numerical divergence; The relationship between the number of restarts, the number of ranks, and the identity of the grid is unclear; After changing the grid, I want to continue calculation from the old Restart; boundary preview shows that the key entrance or exit is empty; mpirun or MPI reports a system-level error; There may be multiple processes writing files in the same calculation example directory at the same time; Both Visit/ and Restart/ are incomplete, but the results need to be restored; It is not sure whether Restart can still be used after forced stop; The log appears with fatal or abort that you cannot determine; Formal calculation results are used in reports, papers or engineering conclusions, but there are exceptions in the process. When contacting please provide the information listed in Section 7.1. The more complete the information, the faster the positioning.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 7.16 Troubleshooting Tips for Beginners You can write down the order of investigation into one sentence: Look at the environment first, then look at the input; do a short test first, then a long run; first warm up, then process; first package, then send; first keep the log, then ask for help. Corresponding to the COAST file is: Environment: doctor; Input: case validate, boundary preview, mesh status; Run: coastctl run --preflight, coastctl run --execute; Monitoring: monitor, screen, external .coast_run_logs/ stdout/stderr; Stop: coastctl stop; Result: Visit/solution.visit plus complete .vtk; Continuation calculation: full Restart/restart.NNN, and if necessary, full restart_pdf.NNN. As long as you follow this order, most problems can be narrowed down to a clear scope instead of searching in a pile of documents. 8. Complete program description of unpackaged version This chapter describes the complete development working directory, which is the current directory: /path/to/Coast_software It is not the same as the “encapsulated carrying case”. The packaged version is mainly for ordinary users to run and view results. It only contains the programs, template calculation examples, graphical auxiliary interfaces, documents and agent skills required for running. The full directory of the unpackaged version also contains source code, test scripts, build files, EXEC examples currently in use, packaging tools and development aids. Ordinary users only need to know: in the unpackaged version, EXEC is the current calculation example and SRC.Coast is the program source code. Subsequent developers and AI agents also need to know that building, checking, grid switching, restart remapping, and packaging and publishing should all be completed through controlled commands in the workspace. Do not manually spell directories or delete data in use. Note: The commands in this chapter are executed on the Linux server by default, and start from the workspace root directory by default: cd /path/to/Coast_software
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.1 What is the complete working directory? The complete working catalog can be understood as COAST’s “maintenance room plus operation room”. Source code, tests, tools, current calculation examples and packaged output are all in the same directory tree, which facilitates development and verification. The core structure of the current workspace is as follows: Coast_software/ SKILL.md README.md workplan.md coastctl coast-ui docs/ USER_MANUAL.md manual_sections/ scripts/ check_layout.sh SRC.Coast/ Makefile app/ parallel/ cpp/ mesh/ physics/ tools/ ui/ tests/ ai/skills/ EXEC/ coast coast_remap input.d ibm_mesh.d boundary_conditions.d vtk_output.d spray.d spark.d probe.d heat_release.d mesh5_auto_refine.d Geometry/ Fuels/ Decomp/ runtime_mesh/ Restart/ Visit/ Info/ codegraphf_portable/ dist/ templates/ tests/ third_party/ The purpose of these directories is as follows: Path Explanation for ordinary users Explanation for development/AI agent SKILL.md General description of the current workspace. After entering the workspace, read it first and then select the sub-skill. workplan.md Description of the current development stage and restricted areas. Current source of truth for Mesh-4/Mesh-5 status, core checks, prohibitions. coastctl Entry to common operation commands. Root directory wrapper, actually calls SRC.Coast/tools/coastctl.py. coast-ui Start the entrance of Chinese graphical auxiliary interface. Root directory wrapper, service code is in SRC.Coast/ui/. docs/ User manuals and documentation. Manual integration, chapter division and published document sources. scripts/ Workspace auxiliary check script. check_layout.sh is used to confirm directory integrity. SRC.Coast/ COAST program source code. Home of Fortran/C++ source code, tools, GUIs, tests and agent skills. EXEC/ The directory where the current calculation example and executable program are located. active case, running input, running output, active grid, Restart, and Visit are all here. codegraphf_portable/ Portable installation package for code retrieval tools. CodeGraphF can be installed after migrating the server. dist/ Portable package output directory. One of the output locations of coastctl package build. third_party/ Third-party dependencies or offline packages. Currently contains OCE/OpenCASCADE related native material. Note: EXEC/ is not the template directory, but the current active calculation example. The Restart/, runtime_mesh/, Decomp/, and Visit/ may contain data that is being used or analyzed and cannot be cleared easily.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.2 Relationship between SRC.Coast and EXEC SRC.Coast and EXEC are the most important pair of directories in the unpackaged version. SRC.Coast is “where the program comes from”. It contains COAST’s Fortran/C++ source code, build files, test scripts, grid and restart tools, GUI backend, packaging tools, and AI agent skills. EXEC is “where the program runs”. It contains the current executable program EXEC/coast, the C++ Restart remapping backend EXEC/coast_remap, the current input files, geometry, fuel, running mesh, Restart data, Visit output and screen. The stdout/stderr, run manifest, and PID/session status of coastctl should be placed outside the calculation in .coast_run_logs/ and should not pollute the EXEC root directory. Common relationships can be written like this: Actions Main Directory Results Modify program source code SRC.Coast/ Affects EXEC/coast after next build. Builder SRC.Coast/ Generate or update ../EXEC/coast and ../EXEC/coast_remap. Change the calculation example parameters EXEC/*.d No need to recompile, but it must be verified before running. Run calculations EXEC/ or ./coastctl run Read EXEC input, write EXEC/screen, Visit/, Restart/, etc.; run-control logs are written to external .coast_run_logs/. Check mesh status ./coastctl mesh status --case-dir EXEC Read EXEC/runtime_mesh, EXEC/Decomp and related identity files. Make the portable package Root directory ./coastctl package build Extract the running package from SRC.Coast and lightweight template, and output it to dist/. NOTE: Do not copy SRC.Coast into the portable runtime package. The portable package should only contain the binaries, template studies, graphical interfaces, documentation, and agent skills required to run it.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.3 What to check first when entering the unpackaged version of the workspace for the first time After entering the workspace, first confirm that the directory and key files are complete: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./scripts/check_layout.sh This command should output something like: COAST layout check cwd=Coast_software present source SRC.Coast active_source=SRC.Coast present case EXEC active_case=EXEC present exec_input EXEC/input.d present exec_input EXEC/boundary_conditions.d ... If you see missing source SRC.Coast or missing case EXEC, it means that the current directory is not a complete workspace, or the directory has been moved/deleted. Do not continue building or running at this time, confirm the path first. You can also use coastctl doctor to do a more operational-level check: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl doctor --case-dir EXEC --json This command will output the inspection results in JSON. Regular users only need to look for obvious error fields; development/AI agents should save or reference key error messages instead of just saying “doctor failed”.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.4 Build program Building means: compiling the source code in SRC.Coast into a executable EXEC/coast. Execute in the root directory of the workspace: cd /path/to/Coast_software cd SRC.Coast make -j 8 test -x ../EXEC/coast test -x ../EXEC/coast_remap The meaning of each step is as follows: Command Effect Expected results cd SRC.Coast Enter the source code directory. The current directory becomes SRC.Coast. make -j 8 Compile the program with 8 parallel tasks. Compilation ends without Error and generates/updates the executable program. test -x ../EXEC/coast Check whether EXEC/coast exists and is executable. The command has no output and returns success. test -x ../EXEC/coast_remap Check whether the C++ Restart remap backend exists and is executable. The command has no output and returns success. If the build fails, first look at the last few dozen lines of errors in the terminal. Common causes include an incomplete compiler environment, incompatible .mod files left over from a previous build, or the source file has just been modified. Don’t delete EXEC/Restart or EXEC/runtime_mesh without read errors, build failures usually have nothing to do with runtime data. Note: The build does not automatically start calculating. Actually running the calculation requires mpirun or coastctl run --execute.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.5 Core check command The following commands are the main line of daily inspection of the unpackaged version. Ordinary users can think of them as “pre-operational physical examinations”. Development/AI agents should perform relevant checks before and after changing code, changing input, changing mesh, or packaging.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Workspace and study inspection cd /path/to/Coast_software ./scripts/check_layout.sh ./coastctl doctor --case-dir EXEC --json ./coastctl case validate --case-dir EXEC --json ./coastctl mesh status --case-dir EXEC --json The meaning is as follows: Commands What to check What to see if normal ./scripts/check_layout.sh Whether the directory and key input exist. present source, present case, present exec_input. ./coastctl doctor --case-dir EXEC --json Running environment and basic status of the calculation example. There are no fatal errors in JSON. ./coastctl case validate --case-dir EXEC --json EXEC/*.d Whether the input file can be recognized by the tool. JSON indicates that the verification is passed. ./coastctl mesh status --case-dir EXEC --json Current mesh source, rank number, active mesh status. Can read runtime_mesh status and rank information.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Boundary and Grid Preview Check cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl boundary preview --case-dir EXEC --write --json ./coastctl mesh preview --case-dir EXEC --write --json boundary preview will preview the entrance, exit, wall and other boundary selections according to EXEC/boundary_conditions.d, and write out boundary_preview.json if necessary. It can help find problems such as “the selection area is empty”, “the boundary is selected to the wrong side”, “the IBM surface inlet does not match the adjacent fluid surface”, etc. mesh preview will generate or update the mesh preview material. Ordinary users usually only need to view pictures through the graphical auxiliary interface; developers can check the written JSON, Visit preview and grid reports.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Graphical auxiliary interface self-test cd /path/to/Coast_software python3 SRC.Coast/ui/coast_ui.py --self-test --workspace . This command does not start a long-term service, but checks whether the graphical interface backend can load the workspace and read the necessary interfaces. If it is normal, it should return success; if it fails, first check whether the error is related to the missing path, Python environment, or input file.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Pre-check before running cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl run --case-dir EXEC --ranks 128 --preflight --json --preflight is a pre-run check and does not mean official startup. It should check whether the rank number, number of Restart files, number of PDF Restart files, number of runtime mesh files, etc. match. Production preflight/execute uses C++ EXEC/coast_remap by default when input.d requests restart-time regrid or rank number needs to be replaced. Python reference will only be used if --remap-backend python-reference is explicitly passed in; when EXEC/coast_remap is not found, an error will be reported and stopped, and no silent rollback will be performed. Note: Only adding --execute will actually start mpirun. For production calculation examples, you must first confirm the step limit, Restart setting, rank number and output position in EXEC/input.d. Note: The normal user command is still cd EXEC && mpirun -np N ./coast. If MPI size differs from the active runtime mesh rank count, and the configuration allows startup regrid / restart remap, the startup phase will take the controlled preflight/write/remap path before the solver reads fields; if the rank, number of files, mesh identity, remap backend or access control conditions are not met, the direct solver will fail to close and write out screen / JSON diagnosis.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Official startup and monitoring Use only when the user explicitly authorizes the real run: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl run --case-dir EXEC --ranks 128 --execute --write --json Monitor the current running status: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl monitor --case-dir EXEC --json tail -80 EXEC/screen Gentle stop: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl stop --case-dir EXEC --json Note: Do not directly kill the process as the preferred stopping method. Use coastctl stop first because it is more consistent with the running convention of the current workspace.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.6 Recommended test collection Below are the core static/workflow checks for Mesh-3, Mesh-4, Restart, Mesh-5 and GUI. Most of them will not initiate long-term real calculations and are suitable for post-development verification. cd /path/to/Coast_software python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh3_runtime_static.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh4_activation_transaction.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_restart_interpolation.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_restart_remap_staging.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_restart_remap_production_static.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh5_nonmatching_static.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh5_auto_refine.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_plan2_full.py If there is Visit output in the current EXEC/Visit and you want to check whether the visualization block junctions are continuous, you can run: cd /path/to/Coast_software/SRC.Coast python3 tests/check_visit_overlap_continuity.py \ /path/to/Coast_software/EXEC/Visit The highlights of these inspections are as follows: Check Script Highlights check_mesh3_runtime_static.py Mesh-3 runtime-conformal Whether the mainline remains available. check_mesh4_activation_transaction.py Whether the Mesh-4 activation, rollback, and identity synchronization processes are protected. check_restart_interpolation.py Restart whether the basic logic of interpolation is correct. check_restart_remap_staging.py Whether the new mesh Restart staging can generate the expected files. check_restart_remap_production_static.py Restart/remap protection cannot be skipped in the production path. check_mesh5_nonmatching_static.py Mesh-5 non-matching interfaces cannot be accidentally opened. check_mesh5_auto_refine.py Whether the automatic local refinement candidate selector works in candidate mode. check_plan2_full.py Plan2/graphical auxiliary interface Whether the relevant workflow remains connected. Note: If a test fails, do not change irrelevant files immediately. Read the failure message first to confirm whether it is checking source code, input files, grid files, or run output.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.7 CodeGraphF assisted retrieval CodeGraphF is a source code navigation tool. It is suitable for answering questions such as “where a certain function is implemented”, “who calls this module”, “how the boundary conditions flow from the input file to the solver”. It is recommended to use wrapper for the current project: ~/.local/bin/cgf-coast Commonly used commands are as follows: cgf-coast status cgf-coast sync cgf-coast query "mpi halo exchange" cgf-coast context --code -n 16 "where boundary_conditions.d inlet velocity is applied" The meaning of the command is as follows: Command When to use Expected results cgf-coast status Before using the search results. Display index status, number of files, number of nodes, or whether synchronization is required. cgf-coast sync After modifying the source code, or when the index is suspected to be out of date. Refresh the index of SRC.Coast. cgf-coast query "<keyword>" Want to quickly find related files/modules/functions. Returns potentially relevant locations. cgf-coast context --code -n <N> "<issue>" Requires context with code snippets. Returns the compact implementation context. The recommended order for developing/AI agents is: For issues regarding architecture, call chain, and implementation location, use cgf-coast first. Use rg for precise text search, log search, and file name search. Don’t read the entire source tree in a large range just to find a function. If the workspace is moved to another server and cgf-coast is not available, a portable copy can be installed: cd /path/to/Coast_software/codegraphf_portable bash install_codegraphf.sh After installation execute: cgf-coast status If the project path changes after migration, you need to check whether PROJECT= in ~/.local/bin/cgf-coast still points to the new SRC.Coast.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.8 How to use AI SKILLs This workspace contains skill files for AI agents. They are not something that ordinary users must learn, but they are very important for subsequent development and automation operations. After entering the workspace, the AI ​​agent should first read the root directory: SKILL.md It explains workspace layout, safe operation strategies, CodeGraphF usage, failure troubleshooting sequences, and common no-go areas. If SRC.Coast/ai/skills/ exists, sub-skills should be selected by task: Skill file Fit for task SRC.Coast/ai/skills/coast-runtime/SKILL.md Build, dry-run, smoke, run commands. SRC.Coast/ai/skills/coast-case-author/SKILL.md Create calculation examples and edit direct input files. SRC.Coast/ai/skills/coast-boundary-authoring/SKILL.md Author or adjust boundary_conditions.d. SRC.Coast/ai/skills/coast-failure-triage/SKILL.md Operation failure, numerical anomaly, log troubleshooting. SRC.Coast/ai/skills/coast-package-release/SKILL.md Build, audit, install and test the portable release package. SRC.Coast/ai/skills/rangeai-coast-portable/SKILL.md Portable package installation, startup graphical interface, short run, monitoring. SRC.Coast/ai/skills/rangeai-coast-case-boundary/SKILL.md *.d in portable package and boundary condition editor. Basic rules for AI agents: First confirm that the current directory is Coast_software. Read SKILL.md first and the sub-skill corresponding to the task. Read the logs and input files first, then change the source code. Do not initiate long real calculations without authorization. Do not delete production Restart/, runtime_mesh/, Decomp/, geometry, fuel or user Visit output to be preserved. When encountering Mesh-4/Mesh-5 mesh related work, first read the current status and restricted areas of workplan.md.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.9 How developers update documentation Draft chapters of this manual are available at: docs/manual_sections/ The main manual is located at: docs/USER_MANUAL.md The recommended approach is: First update the chapter text according to division of labor in docs/manual_sections/. The main agent is unified into docs/USER_MANUAL.md. After integration, check whether the title level, command path, Chinese description and terminology are consistent. Before packaging, confirm that docs/USER_MANUAL.md contains the latest version of the content that needs to be released to users. Ordinary users do not need to maintain these files. When developing/updating documentation for AI agents, you should pay attention to: Full text in Chinese, command block marked bash or powershell. Give Chinese explanations when terms such as COAST/Mesh/Restart/Visit appear for the first time. Write down the execution location, prerequisites and expected results for each dangerous operation. Don’t end your explanation with “See source code for details”. Do not write temporary debugging conclusions as long-term facts.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 8.10 How developers update packages The package must be created through coastctl package build, do not copy the directory manually. The standard process is as follows: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl package build --dist-dir dist/coast_portable_latest \ --version coast-portable-current --archive --force --json ./coastctl package audit \ --package-dir dist/coast_portable_latest/coast-runtime-coast-portable-current-linux-x86_64 \ --json ./coastctl package install-test \ --package-dir dist/coast_portable_latest/coast-runtime-coast-portable-current-linux-x86_64 \ --json The package should contain: coast-runtime-<version>-linux-x86_64/ bin/coast-solver bin/coast_remap bin/coastctl bin/coast-ui env/coast-env.sh ui/static/ docs/USER_MANUAL.md agent_skills/rangeai-coast-portable/SKILL.md agent_skills/rangeai-coast-case-boundary/SKILL.md SKILL.md EXEC_TEMPLATE/ *.d runtime_mesh/ Restart/ manifest.json PACKAGE_AUDIT.json install.sh The wrapper should not contain: Should not contain Reason SRC.Coast/ The source code does not belong to the ordinary running package. .git/ Version history and internal information are not part of the release runtime package. tests/ The test tree will increase the size of the package and is not required for ordinary users to run. CodeGraphF Index Machine path related, easily misleading after migration. EXEC/Restart active data may be large, and is the current workspace running status, not a template. EXEC/Visit active output The resulting file can be large and should not be mixed with clean templates. EXEC/*.log, EXEC/*.json, EXEC/*.pid, session temporary files run-control temporary files should be in .coast_run_logs/, staging or archive directory and should not pollute the template. .F90, .cpp, .mod, .o and other source code/built products The running package only contains necessary running files. Package acceptance must meet at least: package audit passed. package install-test passes and includes coast-ui --self-test. The package contains docs/USER_MANUAL.md, root SKILL.md and two RangeAI agent skills. C++ remap backend included in the package. The package version can provide bin/coast_remap and ensure that coastctl run can find it in the working example or EXEC compatible location; the source version must have EXEC/coast_remap. In-package templates or instructions override necessary *.d configuration, runtime_mesh/ examples, and empty or example Restart/. Packages must not use Python reference remap as a production automatic fallback; production default should be C++ coast_remap, Python reference can only be explicit --remap-backend python-reference. The source code version/package version must have coast, coast_remap, coastctl, necessary .d and directory structure: the source code version corresponds to EXEC/coast, EXEC/coast_remap, SRC.Coast/tools/coastctl.py and EXEC/*.d, and the package version corresponds to bin/coast-solver, bin/coast_remap, bin/coastctl and EXEC_TEMPLATE/*.d. The manifest.json in the package does not mistakenly write Mesh-4 candidate preview as active solver mesh. The startup behavior of coastctl run --execute is still a controlled background mpirun startup and stdin is closed. 9. Description of Grid, Restart and Partial Encryption Methods This chapter explains COAST’s current grid and Restart methods. The average user does not need to understand each underlying algorithm, but does need to know which directories represent the current active state and which are just candidates or previews. Developers and AI agents need to strictly distinguish the responsibilities of Mesh-3, Mesh-4, and Mesh-5 to avoid mistaking candidate files for formal solution meshes.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 9.1 First understand a few basic words A grid divides a continuous calculation area into many small grids. COAST calculates physical quantities such as velocity, pressure, temperature, composition, PDF scalars, etc. on these grids. Restart is restart data. It saves the calculation status of a certain step, and the calculation can be continued from this moment instead of starting from zero. runtime mesh is the runtime mesh. The active mesh actually read by the current solver is: EXEC/runtime_mesh/ Decomp is a compatibility bridge still needed for old initialization code. In the current build/runtime grid mode, EXEC/Decomp should not be treated as manual authoritative input for arbitrary editing. IBM is an immersed boundary method, which can be understood as “immersed boundary method” in Chinese. It uses markers to distinguish fluid regions from solid/wall regions, allowing complex geometries to be embedded in a structured background mesh. The active solver mesh is the mesh that the current solver actually uses for calculations. Candidate meshes, preview meshes, and diagnostic meshes are not active solver meshes.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 9.2 Mesh-3: Stabilizing the main line Mesh-3 is the current stable solution main line, which can be understood as the “runtime consistent mesh” main line. In English, it is often written as runtime_conformal or runtime-conformal. “Conformal” means that the mesh faces of adjacent blocks can be aligned. This is important to the solver because when adjacent MPI blocks exchange boundary data, they can swap paths with existing matching blocks without having to deal with non-matching surfaces of different thicknesses. Key features of Mesh-3: Active mesh from EXEC/runtime_mesh/. EXEC/Decomp/ still exists as a compatibility bridge, but is not a manual authoritative input for new grid work. There are matching interfaces between adjacent blocks and the existing mpi_halo_exchange(field,hhalo) fast path can still be used. Inlet, outlet, and wall boundaries are controlled by EXEC/boundary_conditions.d. STL geometry and coordinate/IBM selectors can work together and do not require that the current STL has a patch tag. The current mesh authority in EXEC/ibm_mesh.d needs to be understood according to the mode: mesh_source Meaning Operation Notes legacy_decomp The hand-prepared EXEC/Decomp is authoritative. Only reasonable if allow_run_from_decomp = .true.. generated_decomp The integrated mesh generator writes out Decomp and uses it as the current source. The build results still have to be checked by the tool. runtime_conformal runtime_mesh is the authority, Decomp is the compatibility bridge. The current main line of thinking, do not manually modify Decomp when repairing. runtime_amr Reserved for true non-matching AMR. Currently not production enabled, code should fail closed. NOTE: Mesh-3’s stability comes from matched blocks and a controlled active mesh. Do not manually copy a candidate directory to EXEC/runtime_mesh for local refinement.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 9.3 Mesh-4: New mesh Restart closed loop The goal of Mesh-4 is not to dynamically refine at any time during the calculation process, but to allow COAST to safely complete this closed loop: Generate a new target mesh -> Preview and check -> Remap the old Restart to the new mesh -> Activate the new runtime_mesh -> Synchronize the Restart identity -> Validate with a short run -> Roll back if necessary Mesh-4/Plan2 in the current workspace is already a closed-loop infrastructure. The current activity status record is: Active solver mesh: EXEC/runtime_mesh Active mesh source: mesh4_axis_spacing_policy Active grid: 109 x 319 x 106 over 128 ranks Active Restart: EXEC/Restart remapped onto the promoted Mesh-4 target Restart identity: Restart/mesh_identity.NNN must match runtime_mesh/mesh_identity.txt Mesh-4 does several key things: Stage Vernacular explanation Key protection Target mesh generation Prepare a new matching run mesh. First as proposal/candidate, it does not directly cover the active grid. Boundary/IBM Remark Re-determine which cells are fluid, solid, inlet, outlet, and wall on the new grid. Prevents loss of boundaries or IBM tags. Restart remapping Move the physical quantities on the old grid to the new grid. Use fluid-solid mask, PDF protection, velocity/enthalpy protection. activation preflight Check the rank number, file number, and identity file before activation. Reject startup if not matched. promotion Switch the target mesh to EXEC/runtime_mesh. Requires synchronization Restart mesh identity. rollback Return to the previous active state when something goes wrong. Preserve recoverable paths. If Mesh-4 promotion or rollback is done manually, the Restart identity must be synchronized: cd /path/to/Coast_software python3 SRC.Coast/tools/mesh4_activation_transaction.py \ sync-restart-identity --exec-dir EXEC Synchronizing identities means: Let each mesh_identity.NNN in EXEC/Restart match the activity EXEC/runtime_mesh/mesh_identity.txt. In this way, when restarting, the solver will not use the Restart of the old grid to configure the new grid. Note: The Mesh-4 candidate preview file still has diagnostic value, but after activation the actual solution mesh only looks at EXEC/runtime_mesh.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 9.4 Restart Vernacular explanation of interpolation and remapping Restart remapping can be understood as “moving the weather values ​​on the old map to the grid on the new map.” The grid positions, sizes, and numbers of the old grid and the new grid may be different. You cannot simply copy restart.000 to the new directory by file name, because the 100th grid may not be at the same spatial position on the old grid and the new grid. Proper remapping requires doing the following: Read the old Restart and old runtime mesh. Read the target runtime mesh. For each target fluid grid, find a reasonable old grid donor. Perform interpolation or protective transfer of fields such as velocity, pressure, temperature, density, composition, PDF scalar, etc. Check the old and new fluid-solid markers to prevent the fluid grid from borrowing values ​​from the solid donor. Write the restart.*, restart_pdf.* and identity/manifest files corresponding to the new grid. The production default tool is C++ EXEC/coast_remap. coastctl run --preflight and coastctl run --execute use this by default; Python reference is only used when --remap-backend python-reference is explicit. coast_remap can also be used staging-only: cd /path/to/Coast_software EXEC/coast_remap \ --restart-dir EXEC/Restart \ --source-runtime-mesh EXEC/Restart/runtime_mesh \ --target-runtime-mesh EXEC/Mesh5.target/runtime_mesh \ --output-dir EXEC/Restart.remapped_mesh5_target \ --overwrite-output \ --allow-solid-to-fluid-nearest-donor \ --progress-file /tmp/coast_remap_progress.log It only writes --output-dir and does not override active EXEC/Restart or EXEC/runtime_mesh. --rank-range A:B or --rank-list 0,4,7 can be used for diagnostic partial staging, but partial rank subset is not promotable and cannot be used in place of active Restart. Common output includes: EXEC/Restart/restart.* EXEC/Restart/restart_pdf.* EXEC/Restart/restart.stat EXEC/Restart/restart_payload_manifest.json EXEC/Restart/restart_remap_manifest.json EXEC/Restart/mesh_identity.NNN EXEC/Restart/runtime_mesh/ Restart remapping check points: Check items Why it matters The number of restart.* is equal to the number of ranks Each MPI rank requires its own Restart input. The number of restart_pdf.* is equal to the number of ranks When PDF Restart is turned on, each rank must have PDF status. Restart/runtime_mesh/ Consistent with the active mesh The Restart run understands the geometry and IBM markup as per that snapshot. mesh_identity.NNN matches runtime_mesh/mesh_identity.txt Prevents the old mesh from being mixed into the new mesh during Restart. manifest file exists to facilitate tracking old meshes, new meshes and transfer methods later. You can use the following command to quickly count files: cd /path/to/Coast_software find EXEC/runtime_mesh -maxdepth 1 -name 'block_*.dat' | wc -l find EXEC/Restart -maxdepth 1 -name 'restart.*' | wc -l find EXEC/Restart -maxdepth 1 -name 'restart_pdf.*' | wc -l If you plan to run with 128 ranks, the above three quantities should be compatible with your current run settings. If read_pdf=true, restart_pdf.* must also match. Common reasons for remap failure include: missing EXEC/coast_remap, inconsistent number of source/target rank or Restart files, failed marker transition gate, --output-dir already exists without --overwrite-output, or --progress-file is placed within --output-dir.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 9.5 Fluid-solid marking protection Fluid-solid markers are the basis for COAST to distinguish between “here is a fluid” and “here is a solid/wall” in the IBM grid. The main conventions currently in the Visit preview are: IBM_marker = 1.0 means fluid IBM_marker = 0.0 means solid Core principles of fluid-solid mark protection: Fluid grids cannot borrow physics values from solid donors. Solid grids cannot be accidentally filled by normal fluid exchange. Fluid to solid and solid to fluid transitions are counted and reported. IBM wall adjacent inlet selection can only work on existing fluid adjacent surfaces. boundary_conditions.d can only select existing fluid boundaries, and cannot force solid grids into fluids. For the average user, this means: If the portal preview is empty, do not blindly “brush out” the portal by expanding parameters. Entry may also be denied by the protection logic if there is only a thin fluid cap near the geometry. source ibmSurface selects the IBM wall surface adjacent to the fluid surface, rather than opening the solid wall. source externalBoundary selects the real outer boundary, not any MPI block surface. For development/AI agents, the following checks are very important: cd /path/to/Coast_software python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_boundary_source_semantics_static.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_ibm_surface_inlet_velocity_model_static.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_inlet_opening_depth_static.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_restart_marker_transition.py These tests maintain several key behaviors: the outer boundary and the inner plane of the block cannot be confused, the direction of the entrance to the IBM surface cannot be chaotic, the entrance must have sufficient connectivity depth, and the Restart remapping cannot ignore fluid-structure conversion.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 9.6 Mesh-5: Automatic local refinement candidates The goal of Mesh-5 is to enable COAST to support true local refinement in the future, specifically where a parent patch is locally refined adjacent to a surrounding coarser mesh. This thing is harder than Mesh-4 because adjacent blocks are no longer always face-to-face aligned. One side of the fine grid may correspond to the side of the coarse grid, with a different number of grids. This is called non-matching block exchange. The solver needs to know how to populate the thick and thin interfaces with ghost cells, protect velocity, pressure, temperature, composition, PDF scalars, and ultimately verify conserved fluxes. Currently, Mesh-5 already has security scaffolding and candidate generation tools: SRC.Coast/tools/mesh5_single_block_refine.py SRC.Coast/tools/mesh5_auto_refine.py EXEC/mesh5_auto_refine.d EXEC/Mesh5.auto_refined_candidate/ The automatic local refinement selector scores candidate parent blocks. Current rating sources include: Indicators Vernacular explanation Geometric Metrics Areas with complex geometry, close to walls or changing boundaries may require finer meshes. Vorticity Index Locations where flow rotation or shear is strong may require finer meshes. Reaction dcdt indicator Locations where the combustion reaction changes rapidly may require a finer mesh. The default configuration file is: EXEC/mesh5_auto_refine.d It is off by default. You can view or run candidate checks first: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl mesh auto-refine --case-dir EXEC --json To generate candidates all at once, you can use: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl mesh auto-refine --case-dir EXEC \ --enable-once --restart-auto-refine --json You can also let the running plan generate candidates before Restart, but do not add --execute and look at the plan first: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl run --case-dir EXEC --ranks 128 \ --auto-refine-restart-candidate --auto-refine-force \ --preflight --write --json Note: automatic local refinement currently generates candidates, that is, candidate packages. The candidate package is not an active solution mesh.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 9.7 Why Mesh-5 candidates cannot be used directly as active solver mesh This is one of the most important safety rules in this chapter: Mesh-5 candidate != active solver mesh You cannot directly copy EXEC/Mesh5.auto_refined_candidate to EXEC/runtime_mesh for the following reasons: Reason Explanation Non-matching exchange is still in the verification stage Thick and thin interfaces require a special halo schedule, and not all production scenarios have been verified. Candidates may change the number of blocks and rank mapping A parent block may be split into 8 child blocks, and the number of Restart files will also change accordingly. The candidate is written with activation access control The current candidate will be marked with a status similar to safe_for_restart_remap_target false, indicating that it cannot be directly promoted to the production grid. Restart has not completed remapping the new target There is no corresponding new mesh Restart, the solver cannot safely continue. Fluid-solid markers and boundaries need to be revalidated IBM markers, entry depth, and boundary selection may all change after local refinement. Conservative fluxes still need to be verified The mass, momentum, enthalpy, and component fluxes of the thick and thin interfaces must eventually be subject to conservation checks. The lack of rollback protection can be dangerous There is no way to reliably return to the last active Mesh-4 state when something goes wrong. Candidate packages can do the following: Show developers where local refinement is appropriate. Generate non-matching interface materials such as interfaces.dat, interface_<rank>.dat and so on. Record parent/child lineage, thickness ratio, marker transition diagnostics. Use test scripts to verify C++ runtime schedule, pack/unpack, coarse-to-fine interpolation, and fine-to-coarse averaging. Candidate packages cannot do these things: Cannot directly replace EXEC/runtime_mesh. You cannot directly configure the old EXEC/Restart to start production solving. Cannot bypass Mesh-4 remap, activation preflight and rollback. Cannot be used as evidence of “Completed Dynamic AMR”.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 9.8 Mesh-5 follow-up goals The long-term goal of Mesh-5 is to build a static, precomputed non-matching block switching layer. It does not do dynamic AMR first, but first allows a local refinement target to run safely. Target capabilities include: A parent block can be refined in one or more directions. When coarse blocks and thin blocks are adjacent, run the grid record thickness interface. ghost cell exchange supports scalar, PDF scalar, density, temperature, pressure and velocity. Interface diagnostics can report maximum jump, average jump, and conservation drift. A refinement parent block can be split into multiple child blocks, for example 8 child blocks of 2 x 2 x 2. Load balancing is estimated by active fluid unit workload, not just by background grid count. Mesh-4’s Restart remap and activation transaction are still responsible for new mesh promotion. Current relevant tests include: cd /path/to/Coast_software python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh5_runtime_schedule_active.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh5_candidate_active_segments.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh5_mpi_active_exchange.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh5_single_block_refine.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh5_synthetic_exchange.py Only when the current case of the matching block is not affected, thick and thin interface exchanges pass, Restart can enter short time stepping, Visit can see the interface diagnosis clearly, and rollback is still available, can Mesh-5 gradually approach production use. 10. Appendix This chapter summarizes commonly used commands, commonly used files, terminology, minimum demonstration process and security cleanup rules.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 10.2 Commonly used files and directory tables File or directory Purpose Can you delete it at will EXEC/input.d Main operation control, Restart, number of steps, output, physical model, etc. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/ibm_mesh.d Geometry, IBM, mesh generation, mesh authority and other settings. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/boundary_conditions.d Inlet, outlet, wall boundary conditions. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/vtk_output.d Visit/VTK output variable selection. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/spray.d Spray and evaporation settings. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/spark.d Ignition source settings. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/probe.d Pressure probe settings. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/heat_release.d Heat release diagnostic settings. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/mesh5_auto_refine.d Mesh-5 automatic local refinement candidate configuration. Not recommended to delete. EXEC/coast The current executable program. Can be restored by rebuilding, but do not delete it on the fly. EXEC/coast_remap C++ Restart remap production backend. The source code version production path must be retained. EXEC/runtime_mesh/ The currently active runtime mesh. Cannot be deleted casually. EXEC/Restart/ Current Restart input/output. Cannot be deleted casually. EXEC/Decomp/ Compatible with bridge and old initialization materials. Cannot be deleted casually. EXEC/Visit/ Visual output. The user can only clear it after confirming that it is not needed. EXEC/Info/ Diagnostic information. After the investigation is completed and it is confirmed that it is not needed, some temporary content can be cleared. EXEC/Geometry/ STL/Geometry input. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/Fuels/ Fuel/chemistry related inputs. Cannot be deleted. EXEC/screen Run screen log. Cannot be deleted during operation; old logs can be cleaned up as needed after archiving. .coast_run_logs/ stdout/stderr, run manifest, PID/session status of coastctl run. After the investigation is completed and confirmed to be unnecessary, it can be archived or cleaned. EXEC/*.log, EXEC/*.json, EXEC/*.pid Run-control temporary files that should not appear in the root directory of EXEC. Confirm the source and whether it is still in use before moving to the archive directory; do not use them as normal output locations. EXEC/Mesh5.auto_refined_candidate/ Mesh-5 automatic refinement candidate package. It can be deleted if it is confirmed that it is only an old candidate and will no longer be analyzed. SRC.Coast/ Source code. Cannot be deleted. docs/USER_MANUAL.md The main manual published to users. Cannot be deleted. docs/manual_sections/ Draft sections. Cannot be deleted. dist/ Packed output. Old packages can be cleared after confirming that they are no longer needed.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 10.3 Glossary of common terms Terminology Chinese explanation COAST Computational fluids/combustion solver for this project. case A case containing input, mesh, geometry, Restart and output. EXEC The currently active calculation example directory. SRC.Coast The current active source code directory. solver Solver refers to the program that actually advances the flow/combustion calculations. coastctl The command line operation entrance of COAST. Graphical auxiliary interface Chinese browser interface, used to view status, change some settings, preview and monitor. Mesh Grid, a computing skeleton that cuts space into small grids. Mesh-3 The current stable runtime-conformal matching block solver mainline. Mesh-4 New target mesh, Restart remapping, activation and rollback closed loop. Mesh-5 The next phase toward local refinement and non-matching block exchange. runtime mesh The mesh actually read when the current solver is running. active solver mesh The active mesh currently participating in the solution. candidate mesh Candidate mesh, which can only be used for inspection or subsequent controlled activation, and cannot be solved directly. Restart Save the calculation status data of a certain step for continued calculation. Restart remap Restart the old grid to the new grid. PDF Restart Restart data related to probability density function. rank MPI parallel process number and quantity unit. MPI Multi-process parallel running mechanism. IBM Immersed boundary method with markers for fluids and solids/walls. fluid marker Fluid marker, usually 1.0 in the current Visit preview. solid marker Solid marker, usually 0.0 in the current Visit preview. halo exchange Adjacent parallel blocks exchange boundary layer data. non-matching exchange Special exchange between grid blocks of different thicknesses. Visit How visualization results are organized, solution.visit references multiple VTK files. *.d files COAST direct input files, usually plain text configurations. preflight Preflight before running, without officially starting the solution. promotion Promote the candidate/target grid to the active grid. rollback Return to the previous set of active grids and Restart after an error.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 10.4 Minimum demonstration process This process is suitable for new developers or new AI agents to confirm that “the workspace can be read, built, checked, and long calculation examples will not be started accidentally.” First step, enter the workspace and check the layout: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./scripts/check_layout.sh Expect to see present source SRC.Coast and present case EXEC. The second step is to check the study input and mesh status: ./coastctl doctor --case-dir EXEC --json ./coastctl case validate --case-dir EXEC --json ./coastctl mesh status --case-dir EXEC --json It is expected that there will be no fatal errors in the JSON and the current mesh/rank information can be read. The third step is to build the program: cd /path/to/Coast_software/SRC.Coast make -j 8 test -x ../EXEC/coast Expect make to succeed, test to have no output and return success. The fourth step is to return to the root directory to do graphical interface self-test and core testing: cd /path/to/Coast_software python3 SRC.Coast/ui/coast_ui.py --self-test --workspace . python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh3_runtime_static.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh4_activation_transaction.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_restart_remap_production_static.py python3 SRC.Coast/tests/check_mesh5_auto_refine.py These commands are expected to return success. If it fails, read the error message and do not delete the running data first. The fifth step is to do pre-run pre-check only: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl run --case-dir EXEC --ranks 128 --preflight --json Expect to see check results for rank, Restart, runtime mesh, etc. This command should not start real calculations. Step 6: If the user explicitly requires a short run, confirm that the number of steps in EXEC/input.d has been limited to the short test range, and then start: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl run --case-dir EXEC --ranks 128 --execute --write --json ./coastctl monitor --case-dir EXEC --json tail -80 EXEC/screen Note: Don’t turn a “minimal demo” into a long production calculation. The maximum number of steps, restart mode, rank number and output retention policy must be confirmed before the short test.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 10.5 Security Cleanup Rules Before cleaning, make sure no calculations are running: pgrep -af 'mpirun|mpiexec|./coast|EXEC/coast' || true If you see that there are still mpirun or coast processes, do not clean them yet. When you need to stop, use: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl stop --case-dir EXEC --json Cleaning rules are divided into three categories.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Content that can be cleaned up after confirmation These are usually external temporary logs, old candidates or old release packages, but it is still recommended to take a look at them: cd /path/to/Coast_software ls -ld .coast_run_logs 2>/dev/null || true find EXEC -maxdepth 1 \( -name '*.log' -o -name '*.json' -o -name '*.pid' \) -print ls -ld EXEC/Mesh5.auto_refined_candidate 2>/dev/null || true ls -ld dist/* 2>/dev/null || true After confirming that it is not needed, you can archive the external .coast_run_logs/ or the .log/.json/.pid mistakenly placed in the EXEC root directory to a user-specified location. Do not delete real files by default in the documentation process; old package directories, old candidate directories, and old isolated run directories can only be deleted after confirming that they are no longer used for reproduction, auditing, or comparison.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Don’t clean up the content casually The following directories and files should not be deleted without explicit authorization: EXEC/Restart/ EXEC/runtime_mesh/ EXEC/Decomp/ EXEC/Geometry/ EXEC/Fuels/ EXEC/*.d EXEC/coast EXEC/coast_remap SRC.Coast/ docs/ Special attention: EXEC/Restart/ may be the only entry for continuation. EXEC/runtime_mesh/ is the currently active solver mesh. EXEC/Decomp/ is still a compatibility bridge and cannot be deleted just because it “looks old”. EXEC/Geometry/ and EXEC/Fuels/ are geometry and chemistry inputs. EXEC/*.d is a direct input file, not a temporary file. EXEC/coast and EXEC/coast_remap are the solver and C++ remap production backends respectively.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Cleaning of Visit output EXEC/Visit/solution.visit itself is just an index file, which references many solution.<step>.domain.<rank>.vtk files. Deleting just .visit or just deleting VTK will make the result incomplete. Estimate the size before cleaning Visit: cd /path/to/Coast_software du -sh EXEC/Visit find EXEC/Visit -maxdepth 1 -type f | wc -l It can only be cleared if the user confirms that the results have been archived or are no longer needed. It is best to create an archive or clearly record the reason for deletion before cleaning.
title: COAST User Manual

content: Organize into a clean workspace before transplantation If the goal is to move the unpackaged workspace to another machine, it is recommended to retain these directories and files: SRC.Coast/ EXEC/ docs/ scripts/ templates/ tests/ codegraphf_portable/ dist/coast_portable_latest/ README.md SKILL.md where EXEC/ should only retain the current program and reusable study assets, for example: EXEC/coast EXEC/*.d EXEC/Geometry/ EXEC/Fuels/ EXEC/runtime_mesh/ EXEC/Decomp/ EXEC/injector/ EXEC/chemistry_accel_variants/ EXEC/Probes/ EXEC/SPRAYs/ This content should generally not be mixed in the clean migration directory, unless the user explicitly wants to take away historical results or renew the archive: EXEC/Restart/ EXEC/Visit/ EXEC/imbmesh/ EXEC/screen EXEC/monitor/ EXEC/Mesh*.candidate/ EXEC/Mesh5.*target/ EXEC/Restart.remapped*/ EXEC/*.log EXEC/*.json EXEC/*.pid EXEC/fort.* A safer approach is to “move out” rather than delete directly. For example: mkdir -p /path/to/Coast_software_archives/exec_cleanup_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS mv EXEC/Restart EXEC/Visit EXEC/screen /path/to/Coast_software_archives/exec_cleanup_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS/ 2>/dev/null || true This workspace has been cleaned up on 2026-06-23 according to the above principles: the solver has been stopped, EXEC/Restart, EXEC/Visit, old candidate mesh, remap Restart, monitoring output and ad hoc reports have been moved to: /home/wyf/code_dev/Coast_software_archives/exec_cleanup_20260623_111259 Therefore, the current EXEC is a “clean run asset catalog”, not a “directly renewable catalog”. If EXEC/input.d is still in restart mode, the matching Restart/ must be restored before re-running, or the input must be changed to a fresh-start/reignition path, and the rank number, grid identity and boundary settings must be reconfirmed. Special note: In this long-term measurement that was stopped, the flame was not stably anchored near the reflow area, which cannot be used as a stable combustion acceptance conclusion. Subsequently, it is necessary to recheck the ignition position, fuel/air boundary, local grid and chemical acceleration settings, and then do a new stability verification.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 10.6 Failure troubleshooting sequence When the operation fails or the result is abnormal, it is recommended to read in the following order: ./coastctl monitor --case-dir EXEC --json, especially stdoutLog, stderrLog and errorSummary. stdout/stderr and run manifest pointed to by monitor in external .coast_run_logs/. EXEC/screen, this is the main screen log. EXEC/input.d, EXEC/boundary_conditions.d, EXEC/vtk_output.d, EXEC/spray.d, EXEC/spark.d, EXEC/probe.d, EXEC/heat_release.d. EXEC/ibm_mesh.d and the current EXEC/runtime_mesh/ state. SRC.Coast/ source code. Look at the end of the log: cd /path/to/Coast_software ./coastctl monitor --case-dir EXEC --json tail -120 EXEC/screen The actual files for stdout/stderr are read from the stdoutLog and stderrLog fields in the monitor output. Before changing the source code of the development/AI agent, the failure phenomenon, last log, input settings and current mesh/Restart status should be recorded. Many failures come from input, rank number, Restart file number, empty boundary selection, or mesh identity mismatch, and do not necessarily require changes to the solver source code.
title: COAST User Manual

content: 10.7 The last few red lines These rules bear repeating: Do not restore old boffin, config_boffin, coast-solver, coast-solver-TCR names to active source, script or executable paths. Do not treat the Mesh-4 candidate preview file as the active solution mesh. Do not copy Mesh-5 auto-refinement candidates directly into EXEC/runtime_mesh. Do not enable mesh_regrid.mode='dynamic' or mode='conservative_transfer' for production runs. Do not use boundary_conditions.d to force a solid grid into a fluid. Do not initiate a Restart run without confirming that the rank, Restart, PDF Restart, and runtime mesh file numbers match. Do not remove EXEC/Restart, EXEC/runtime_mesh, EXEC/Decomp or EXEC/screen while running. Do not package the running directory manually, you must use coastctl package build. By adhering to these red lines, the unpackaged version of the workspace can simultaneously serve normal operation, development verification, AI agent collaboration, and portable release. [2] Wang Y, Wang F, Lei S, et al. Dual-modification transported probability density function framework for hydrogen combustion simulation: Resolving differential diffusion effects[J]. Physics of Fluids, 2025, 37(4). [3] Wang Y, Wang F, Zhou J, et al. An improved immersed boundary method with local flow pattern reconstruction and its validation[J]. Physics of Fluids, 2024, 36(4).
title: COAST User Manual

content: COmbustor Adaptive Simulation Toolkit 燃烧室自适应仿真工具中文用户手册 本手册介绍COmbustor Adaptive Simulation Toolkit(COAST)使用。前半部分主要讲封装版便携程序如何通过 SSH 命令行安装、修改算例、运行计算和查看结果；后半部分介绍非封装版完整工作区、网格/重启动/局部加密方法以及开发维护流程。图形辅助界面是单独的辅助设施，一般不作为主线操作方式。 本文件由 docs/manual_sections/ 下的章节草稿整合生成；如果后续要大幅修改某一章，建议先修改对应章节草稿，再重新整合。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 第 1 页：封装版环境配置与 coast-assistant 封装版适合“拿到一个已经打好的运行包，然后在 Linux 服务器上运行算例”的用户。常见目录名类似： coast-runtime-<version>-linux-x86_64/ 封装版通常已经带好求解器、coastctl、coast_remap、模板算例、文档、WebUI 和 nanobot 运行资产。新环境中先确认服务器是 Linux x86_64，并且能找到 python3 和 mpirun： which python3 which mpirun 解压后进入封装包根目录。如果你选择原地运行，可以直接使用包内工具： cd coast-runtime-<version>-linux-x86_64 bin/coast-assistant --self-test --require-runtime --json bin/coast-assistant --configure-model bin/coast-assistant 如果你选择安装到固定位置，可以运行： ./install.sh /opt/coast/runtime source /opt/coast/runtime/env/coast-env.sh coast-assistant bin/coast-assistant 是封装版的新手入口。它不是求解器本体，而是一个助手启动器：它会调用包内的 COAST MCP 工具，帮助你检查算例、阅读和修改输入文件、查看网格和边界、做运行前检查、启动受控短运行、监看 screen 和运行日志。需要浏览器界面时，可以让 assistant 打开 WebUI；WebUI 左侧是聊天，右侧是文件和运行工作台。 封装版中，如果通过 assistant/nanobot 启动真实求解器，仍然要遵守安全流程：先 preflight，再确认启动，再监看进程、screen 和 monitor。不要让 assistant 用普通 shell 命令绕过受控流程去启动 solver；如果不用 assistant，请按本手册运行章节的普通手工命令操作。遇到其他问题，例如“怎么改入口温度”“为什么 preflight 不通过”“screen 里这段错误是什么意思”“如何下载 Visit 结果”，都可以直接问 coast-assistant，让它先用项目内工具检查后再给建议。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 第 2 页：源码版环境配置与 coast-assistant 源码版适合需要重新编译、改源码、同步 compilableCode、调试工具或准备新封装包的用户。常见目录是完整工作区或可编译源码树，例如： Coast_software/ compilableCode/ 源码版不是只拷贝一个可执行文件就能工作。它需要保留 SRC.Coast/、EXEC/、docs/、scripts/、third_party/ 和根目录下的工具入口。新环境中先检查编译和运行依赖： which python3 which make which g++ which mpif90 which mpicxx which mpirun 进入源码版根目录后，先做布局检查： cd compilableCode chmod +x coastctl coast-ui coast-assistant scripts/*.sh ./scripts/check_layout.sh ./scripts/print_quickstart.sh 需要重新编译时，在 SRC.Coast 下执行： cd SRC.Coast make clean make -j"$(nproc)" cd .. 编译成功后，主要产物在： EXEC/coast EXEC/coast_remap 源码版的 ./coast-assistant 不是 make 编译出来的二进制，而是源码树自带的启动脚本。它会调用 SRC.Coast/tools/coast_assistant.py 和同目录工具。首次使用时运行： ./coast-assistant --self-test --json ./coast-assistant --configure-model ./coast-assistant 源码版中，普通用户手工运行入口仍是： cd EXEC mpirun -np N ./coast nanobot/assistant 启动 solver 时则必须走 coast_run_preflight，再走 coast_run_short(confirm=true)，启动后监看 process、screen 和 monitor。源码版里遇到编译失败、依赖缺失、EXEC 配置不明、mesh/restart 状态不清、测试该跑哪些、是否可以打包等问题，也可以先问 ./coast-assistant。它会优先阅读项目说明和受控工具输出，再告诉你下一步怎么做。 0. 手册导读 欢迎使用COAST。本手册面向第一次接触COAST的使用者来写，默认读者不需要有编程基础，也不需要先学会计算流体、燃烧、并行计算或 Linux 系统管理。你只需要知道自己要做的是：通过 SSH 登录 Linux 服务器，准备一个算例，检查设置，用命令行运行计算，然后查看结果。 这一部分负责最前面的入门内容，主要讲封装版，也就是便携运行包的使用方式。如果你手里拿到的是一个已经打包好的 coast-runtime-<version>-linux-x86_64 目录，可以先从这里开始。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 0.1 这份手册适合谁 这份手册适合以下用户： 想先把COAST跑起来，了解算例从准备、运行到查看结果的流程； 需要在 Windows 电脑上通过 SSH 命令行操作 Linux 服务器上的COAST； 不想一开始就接触源码、编译、测试脚本和开发目录； 想知道 EXEC_TEMPLATE、*.d、Restart、Visit、端口转发这些词到底是什么意思； 后续可能会修改边界条件、运行计算、导出结果，但现在先要完成第一次上手。 注意：这不是开发者源码说明。你可以先不用理解 Fortran、MPI、湍流模型、燃烧机理这些技术细节。新手最重要的是分清“哪些文件可以复制和修改，哪些目录不能随便删”。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 0.2 推荐新手先走哪条路径 新手推荐使用封装版的 SSH 命令行路径： 在 Windows 端用 SSH 登录 Linux 服务器。 在 Linux 服务器上解压COAST便携包。 复制 EXEC_TEMPLATE，创建自己的工作算例。 用文本编辑器或命令行工具修改 *.d 设置文件。 用命令行检查算例、边界和网格。 用 coastctl run --preflight 做启动前检查，再用 coastctl run --execute 启动计算。 用 coastctl monitor、screen、外部 .coast_run_logs/ 日志和 Visit/ 查看运行状态与结果。 如果确实需要图形化预览，再单独启动图形辅助界面；它不是主线运行方式。 这条路径的好处是：你不需要编译程序，也不需要在本机安装完整开发环境。便携包已经包含运行所需的 coast-solver 可执行程序、命令行辅助工具、干净算例模板和必要文档。 便携包还提供 nanobot assistant 作为可选新手助手。浏览器方式运行 bin/coast-nanobot-webui --package-root .，左侧是对话，右侧是 COAST 工作台，可做上传、文件查看/编辑/下载、运行前检查、短跑、监看、停止和日志 tail；终端方式运行 bin/coast-nanobot-chat --package-root .。assistant 只应通过 COAST MCP 工具操作，真实运行前必须先通过 preflight，并且需要明确确认。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 0.3 封装版和非封装版有什么区别 COAST有两种常见形态：封装版和非封装版。它们是面向不同用途的两个程序形态：封装版用于日常运行算例，非封装版用于源码开发、编译、测试和维护。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 0.3.1 封装版是什么 封装版也叫便携运行包，通常是一个这样的目录： coast-runtime-<version>-linux-x86_64/ SKILL.md bin/coast-solver bin/coast_remap bin/coastctl bin/coast-ui bin/coast-mcp bin/coast-standard-test bin/coast-nanobot-chat bin/coast-nanobot-webui env/coast-env.sh EXEC_TEMPLATE/ ui/static/ docs/USER_MANUAL.md docs/COAST_NANOBOT_ASSISTANT.md nanobot/ agent_skills/ manifest.json PACKAGE_AUDIT.json install.sh 可以把封装版理解成“已经整理好的运行工具箱”。里面有： bin/coast-solver：COAST的求解器本体，真正做计算的程序； bin/coast_remap：C++ Restart 重映射后端，coastctl run 在需要把旧 Restart 准备到新 runtime mesh 时默认使用它； bin/coastctl：命令行操作工具，用来检查算例、查看网格状态、启动运行、监控和停止； bin/coast-ui：可选图形辅助界面后端，一般不作为主线运行方式； bin/coast-nanobot-webui 和 bin/coast-nanobot-chat：可选 nanobot assistant 入口，分别用于浏览器左 chat/右 workbench 和终端对话； bin/coast-mcp 和 bin/coast-standard-test：assistant 和标准检查使用的 受控工具入口； env/coast-env.sh：环境设置脚本，用来告诉当前终端在哪里找COAST工具； EXEC_TEMPLATE/：干净的算例模板，应该复制后再使用； docs/：说明文档； agent_skills/：给自动化助手使用的操作说明。 封装版通常不包含完整源码、开发测试目录、很大的 Restart 数据或很大的 Visit 结果。普通用户日常运行算例时，不需要这些内容。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 0.3.2 非封装版是什么 非封装版是完整开发工作区，通常类似： Coast_software/ SKILL.md docs/ scripts/ tests/ SRC.Coast/ EXEC/ 非封装版包含源码、测试、工具脚本和默认开发算例。它适合开发者、维护者或需要重新编译 COAST 的用户。比如： 修改 COAST 程序源码； 重新构建开发版主可执行程序； 运行开发测试； 打包新的封装版； 调试网格、重启动、并行交换等底层方法。 注意：如果你只是要运行已有算例、修改输入文件、看结果，新手阶段不建议直接从非封装版开始。非封装版能做的事情更多，也更容易误删或误改关键文件。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 0.3.3 两者如何选择 如果你拿到的是封装包，并且目标是“把算例跑起来”，请使用封装版。 如果你需要修改程序源码、重新编译 COAST，或者有人明确要求你在 SRC.Coast、tests、scripts 里工作，再使用非封装版。 一个简单判断方法： 你想做什么 推荐使用 第一次试用 COAST 封装版 创建自己的工作算例 封装版 用浏览器编辑算例设置 封装版 检查边界和网格 封装版 启动有限步数的计算 封装版 查看 Visit 输出 封装版 修改 COAST 源码 非封装版 重新编译程序 非封装版 打包新的运行包 非封装版
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 0.4 阅读本手册时要记住的安全原则 第一，不要直接修改 EXEC_TEMPLATE。它是干净模板，应该保留原样。每次做演示、测试或正式计算，都先复制一份工作算例，例如 EXEC.demo、EXEC.my_case。 第二，不要随便删除用户算例里的这些目录： Restart/ runtime_mesh/ Decomp/ Geometry/ Visit/ 这些目录可能保存重启动数据、运行网格、并行分区、几何文件和结果文件。删掉之后，有些计算可能无法续算，有些结果可能无法再打开。 第三，不要一上来就启动长时间正式计算。推荐先做短步数测试，确认算例能正常启动、边界没有明显错误、输出目录正常，再做正式计算。 第四，Windows 浏览器访问 Linux 服务器上的 COAST 图形界面 时，通常需要 SSH 端口转发。浏览器地址看起来是 127.0.0.1，但真正的程序运行在 Linux 服务器上。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 0.5 常用术语速查
title: COAST 用户手册

content: COAST COAST 是计算程序的名字。它负责读取算例设置、网格、边界条件和初始数据，然后进行流动、燃烧或相关物理过程的数值计算。 在封装版中，真正执行计算的程序通常是： bin/coast-solver
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 算例 算例就是“一次计算任务的文件夹”。它里面放着这次计算需要的输入文件、网格信息、边界条件、重启动数据和输出结果。 封装版里的 EXEC_TEMPLATE 是模板算例。你应该复制它，得到自己的工作算例，例如： EXEC.demo/ EXEC.engine_test/ EXEC.case001/
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 网格 网格是把计算空间切成许多小格子的方式。COAST 不是直接在连续空间里计算，而是在这些小格子上逐步计算速度、压力、温度、组分等量。 可以把网格理解成“计算用的坐标纸”。格子越细，越能描述复杂结构，但计算量也越大。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 边界 边界是计算区域的外壳或内部固体表面。常见边界包括入口、出口和壁面。 入口：流体从这里进入计算区域； 出口：流体从这里离开计算区域； 壁面：流体不能穿过去的固体表面； IBM 表面：由浸入边界方法识别出的复杂几何表面。 边界条件就是告诉 COAST：“这个边界上应该是什么物理状态”。例如入口速度是多少、温度是多少、出口压力怎么处理、壁面是否无滑移。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: Restart Restart 是重启动数据目录。它保存某个时刻的计算状态，让 COAST 可以从这个状态继续算，而不是每次都从头开始。 可以把 Restart 理解成游戏存档。没有存档时只能从最初状态开始；有存档时可以从中间继续。 注意：Restart 文件通常和并行计算的 rank 数有关。普通用户的直接命令仍是 cd EXEC && mpirun -np N ./coast。如果 MPI size differs from the active runtime mesh rank count，且 input.d 和 Mesh-5 配置允许 startup regrid / restart remap，启动阶段会在 solver reads fields 之前走受控 preflight/write/remap 路径，并把简要诊断写入 screen。如果 rank、Restart 文件、mesh identity、remap 后端或门禁条件不满足，启动会失败关闭并保留诊断，而不是半自动进入求解。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: Visit Visit 是结果输出目录，也常指 VisIt 可视化软件使用的一组结果文件。COAST 通常会生成： Visit/solution.visit Visit/solution.<step>.domain.<rank>.vtk 其中 solution.visit 像一个目录清单，里面引用了很多 .vtk 分块结果文件。只复制 solution.visit 通常不够，必须一起带上它引用的 .vtk 文件。 注意：这里的 Visit 目录和 VisIt 软件名字相关。手册里保留 Visit 这个专有名词。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 服务器 服务器通常指运行 COAST 的 Linux 机器。它可能是一台远程高性能计算节点、一台工作站，或者实验室里的 Linux 主机。 COAST 计算通常在 Linux 服务器上运行，因为计算量大、依赖 Linux 环境，并且可能需要多个 CPU 核心或 MPI 并行。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 图形辅助界面 图形辅助界面 是浏览器界面。COAST 的封装版提供中文 图形辅助界面，让你不用直接记很多命令，也能查看算例状态、修改常用 *.d 文件、预览边界和网格、监控运行、整理 Visit 输出。 图形辅助界面 后端在 Linux 服务器上启动，Windows 用户通过浏览器访问。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 端口 端口是网络服务的门牌号。COAST 图形辅助界面 默认示例使用 18765 端口。 如果 图形辅助界面 启动在服务器的 127.0.0.1:18765，意思是：服务器本机的 18765 端口上有一个只允许本机访问的网页服务。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 端口转发 端口转发是 SSH 提供的一种“安全通道”。它可以把 Windows 电脑上的某个本地端口，连接到 Linux 服务器上的某个端口。 例如： ssh -N -L 18765:127.0.0.1:18765 user@server 意思是：在 Windows 本机打开 127.0.0.1:18765 时，SSH 会把访问转送到服务器上的 127.0.0.1:18765。 这就是为什么浏览器里输入的是本机地址，但看到的是服务器上 COAST 图形界面 的页面。 1. 第一次认识 COAST 本章用不依赖专业背景的方式说明 COAST 的基本工作方式。你不需要马上记住所有术语，只要先知道每个东西大概负责什么。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 1.1 COAST 在一次计算中做什么 一次 COAST 计算大致可以想成下面这条流程： 读取算例文件 -> 读取或生成网格 -> 识别边界和几何 -> 读取初始状态或 Restart -> 按时间步推进计算 -> 定期写出 Restart 和 Visit 结果 也就是说，COAST 需要几个关键输入： 算例设置：这次要算多久、输出频率是多少、使用哪些物理模型； 网格：计算区域如何被切成小格子； 边界条件：入口、出口、壁面分别怎么处理； 初始状态：从头开始，还是从某个 Restart 存档继续； 运行资源：用多少 rank 并行计算。 计算过程中，COAST 会写出结果： screen 或相关日志：运行时的文字信息； Restart/：可继续计算的存档； Visit/：可视化结果； 其他诊断文件：例如探针、热释放或统计输出。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 1.2 一个算例是什么 一个算例就是一个完整的工作文件夹。你可以把它理解成一个项目文件夹，里面包含这次计算需要的一切。 封装版里有一个模板： EXEC_TEMPLATE/ 你不应该直接在模板上运行正式计算，而是复制一份： EXEC.demo/ 复制后的 EXEC.demo 就是你的工作算例。你后续编辑 input.d、boundary_conditions.d、启动计算、生成结果，都发生在这个工作算例里。 一个典型工作算例可能长这样： EXEC.demo/ input.d ibm_mesh.d boundary_conditions.d vtk_output.d spray.d spark.d probe.d heat_release.d Geometry/ Decomp/ Restart/ runtime_mesh/ Visit/ screen 不是每个算例一开始都有全部目录。有些目录会在生成网格、启动计算或写出结果后出现。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 1.3 *.d 文件是什么 COAST 的很多输入设置放在以 .d 结尾的文本文件里，例如： 文件 主要用途 input.d 控制重启动、总步数、输出间隔、燃烧和求解器常用设置 ibm_mesh.d 控制几何、网格、IBM 扫描和静态网格相关设置 boundary_conditions.d 设置入口、出口、壁面、坐标选择器和组分 vtk_output.d 设置 Visit/VTK 输出哪些结果字段 spray.d 喷雾和蒸发相关设置 spark.d 点火源相关设置 probe.d 压力探针相关设置 heat_release.d 热释放诊断相关设置 这些文件是普通文本文件，可以用编辑器打开。封装版的 图形辅助界面 会把其中一些常用设置做成表单，减少手工编辑出错的机会。 注意：能打开并不表示可以随便改。新手阶段建议先通过 图形辅助界面 修改常用项，或者严格按照后续章节说明修改。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 1.4 网格为什么重要 COAST 计算的是流体在空间和时间中的变化。计算机不能直接处理无限连续的空间，所以要先把区域切成很多小单元，这些小单元就是网格。 网格会影响： 计算能否识别几何形状； 入口、出口和壁面的位置是否正确； 结果是否足够细致； 计算速度和内存占用； Restart 是否能继续使用。 如果网格太粗，细小结构可能看不清。如果网格太细，计算可能非常慢。对新手来说，第一次上手不需要自己设计复杂网格，先学会查看网格状态和预览边界更重要。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 1.5 边界为什么重要 边界条件告诉 COAST 计算区域和外界如何相连。即使网格正确，边界条件写错，计算也可能失败或得到没有物理意义的结果。 常见例子： 入口速度方向写反，流体可能从出口方向流入； 出口没有正确设置，压力波可能反射； 壁面漏设，流体可能穿过本该是固体的区域； 组分名字写错，燃烧计算可能找不到对应物种。 封装版支持通过 boundary_conditions.d 设置边界。它还支持坐标选择边界，也就是用空间范围来指定哪些外边界格子属于入口、出口或壁面。这样即使没有 patch STL 标签，也可以设置常见边界。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 1.6 Restart 为什么像“存档” 长时间计算不适合每次从头开始。COAST 会把某些时刻的状态写到 Restart/ 目录，下次可以从那里继续。 Restart 里通常包括每个并行 rank 对应的数据。rank 可以先理解成“并行计算时分出来的工作份数”。如果一个算例用 128 个 rank 运行，COAST 可能把数据分成 128 份。 这也是为什么续算时要特别注意 rank 数。rank 数、网格、Restart 文件数量不匹配时，COAST 可能无法启动。 注意：不要因为 Restart/ 很大就直接删除。删除前必须确认不再需要续算，或者已经另存备份。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 1.7 Visit 结果为什么不能只发一个文件 COAST 的 Visit 输出一般不是单个结果文件，而是一组文件。 常见结构是： Visit/ solution.visit solution.000010.domain.000000.vtk solution.000010.domain.000001.vtk solution.000010.domain.000002.vtk ... solution.visit 像目录清单，告诉 VisIt 软件每个时间步对应哪些 .vtk 文件。真正的大量数据在 .vtk 文件里。 所以分享结果时，不能只发送： Visit/solution.visit 还需要一起发送它引用的 .vtk 文件。否则别人打开时可能只看到空结果或报错。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 1.8 为什么通常需要 Linux 服务器和 Windows 端连接 很多用户的日常电脑是 Windows，而 COAST 运行环境通常在 Linux 服务器上。这是因为： COAST 计算量大，适合在服务器或工作站上运行； 并行计算、MPI、运行脚本和文件权限在 Linux 上更常见； 服务器可能有更多 CPU 核心、更大内存和更稳定的长时间运行环境。 但用户并不一定要坐在服务器前面。常见工作方式是： Windows 电脑 浏览器打开 图形辅助界面 PowerShell 建立 SSH 端口转发 | | 安全连接 v Linux 服务器 解压 COAST 便携包 保存算例文件 启动 coast-ui 运行 COAST 计算 这样做的效果是：计算留在服务器上，操作界面显示在 Windows 浏览器里。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 1.9 常见目录结构图 假设你把封装包放在 Linux 服务器的固定目录下，目录可能是这样： /opt/coast/coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64/ bin/ coast-solver coast_remap coastctl coast-ui env/ coast-env.sh EXEC_TEMPLATE/ input.d ibm_mesh.d boundary_conditions.d vtk_output.d EXEC.demo/ input.d ibm_mesh.d boundary_conditions.d vtk_output.d Restart/ Visit/ docs/ USER_MANUAL.md 其中： coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64/ 是封装包根目录； EXEC_TEMPLATE/ 是模板，不要直接改； EXEC.demo/ 是复制出来的工作算例，可以按任务修改； bin/ 里是运行工具； env/ 里是环境脚本； docs/ 里是文档。 2. 封装版快速上手 本章从一个新用户的角度，完整走一遍封装版的首次使用流程。命令会说明在哪里执行、执行后应该看到什么。 为了方便说明，下面假设： Linux 服务器用户名是 user； Linux 服务器地址是 server； COAST 便携包文件名类似 coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64.tar.gz； 解压后的目录叫 coast-runtime-2026.06-linux-x86_64； 工作算例叫 EXEC.demo； 图形辅助界面 使用端口 18765。 实际使用时，请把 user、server、版本号和路径替换成你的真实信息。
title: COAST 用户手册

content: 2.1 准备 Linux 服务器终端 首先登录 Linux 服务器。可以使用 Windows PowerShell： ssh user@server 这条命令在 Windows PowerShell 中执行。user 是服务器用户名，server 是服务器地址，可以是主机名或 IP 地址。 执行后，如果是第一次连接，PowerShell 可能询问是否信任服务器指纹。确认地址无误后输入 yes。随后输入服务器密码或使用密钥登录。 登录成功后，你会看到 Linux 命令提示符，后续解压和启动 图形辅助界面 的命令都在这个 Linux 终端里执行。
title: COAST 用户手册
